definition_zh: 生物化学；生物体的化学过程与化学组成
definition_en: the science of the chemical processes and substances of living organisms
core_image: 把一只活细胞拆成一张分子反应清单
scene: 两份血检报告摊在桌上，钾的数值低得显眼。 Her biochemistry results showed low potassium after two weeks of illness.
sceneCN: 这里 biochemistry 指「生化检验结果」（第 8 个义项：一组血液化学指标）；句意：患病两周后，她的生化结果显示血钾偏低。

pos.zh: 生物化学；生物体的化学过程；生化检验指标（作不可数名词，指学科或过程时一般不加 -s）

senses.title: The discipline
senses.definition: the branch of science that studies the chemical processes and substances of living organisms
senses.definitionCN: 研究生物体内化学过程与化学物质的学科
senses.example: Biochemistry sits between biology and chemistry on the university campus.
senses.exampleCN: 在大学里，生物化学处在生物学与化学之间。
senses.why: The suffix -istry names a field of study, so the compound first of all labels a discipline with two parent sciences.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -istry 表示研究领域，因此这个词首先命名一门由两门母科学交叉而成的学科。

senses.title: The processes in a body
senses.definition: the chemical processes that take place in a living organism
senses.definitionCN: 活生物体内发生的化学过程
senses.example: The biochemistry of the insect changes sharply when it enters hibernation.
senses.exampleCN: 这种昆虫进入休眠时，其体内的化学过程会发生剧烈变化。
senses.why: The same noun can name not only the study but also its object, because a science and the processes it studies are habitually spoken of with one word.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既可以是学科，也可以是研究对象，因为人们习惯用一个词同时指「学问」和「这门学问所研究的那些过程」。

senses.title: Chemical makeup
senses.definition: the chemical composition of a tissue, organism or substance
senses.definitionCN: 某组织、生物或物质的化学组成
senses.example: The biochemistry of the seed oil makes it suitable for cold climates.
senses.exampleCN: 这种种子油的化学组成使它适合寒冷气候。
senses.why: If processes are the verbs of a cell, the substances are its nouns; the word extends naturally from what happens to what is there.
senses.whyCN: 如果化学过程是细胞里的动词，那么化学物质就是名词；词义从「发生什么」自然延伸到「有什么」。

senses.title: A course or subject
senses.definition: a course, textbook or examination subject dealing with the chemistry of life
senses.definitionCN: 讲授生命化学的课程、教材或考试科目
senses.example: Biochemistry is a required course for medical students here.
senses.exampleCN: 生物化学是这里医学生的必修课。
senses.why: Academic institutions name subjects after the discipline, so the word also labels the thing taught and examined.
senses.whyCN: 学术机构用学科名来命名科目，于是这个词也指被讲授、被考试的那门课。

senses.title: Department or laboratory
senses.titleCN: 生物化学系；生化实验室
senses.definition: an academic department or research unit devoted to the subject
senses.definitionCN: 从事该学科的系或研究单位
senses.example: The biochemistry at this hospital runs the newborn screening programme.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院的生化科负责新生儿筛查项目。
senses.why: A metonymy turns the discipline into the place and the staff that practise it, a pattern common to names of departments.
senses.whyCN: 这是一种转喻：用学科名指从事该学科的场所与人员，院系名称普遍采用这种说法。

senses.title: Clinical branch
senses.definition: the branch that measures chemical substances in patients' samples to diagnose and monitor disease
senses.definitionCN: 测定患者样本中的化学物质以诊断和监测疾病的分支
senses.example: Clinical biochemistry detected the salt imbalance before symptoms appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 临床生物化学在症状出现前就检出了盐类失衡。
senses.why: Medicine split off a service-oriented branch, and the parent word now covers both the pure science and its hospital application.
senses.whyCN: 医学分出一个面向服务的分支，母词于是同时涵盖纯科学与医院里的应用。

senses.title: Chemistry of a pathway
senses.titleCN: 某条代谢通路的生化机制
senses.definition: the specific reactions and molecules of one metabolic route
senses.definitionCN: 某一代谢通路的具体反应与分子
senses.example: The biochemistry of fat storage explains why the liver enlarges.
senses.exampleCN: 脂肪储存的生化机制解释了肝脏为何增大。
senses.why: With of plus a named process, the noun narrows to the chemistry that belongs to that process alone.
senses.whyCN: 当它与表示某个具体过程的词组成介词短语连用时，这个名词就收窄为「该过程专属的那套化学」。

senses.title: Laboratory results
senses.definition: in clinical speech, the set of chemical measurements reported for a patient
senses.definitionCN: 临床上指为患者报告的一组化学测定结果
senses.example: Her biochemistry was normal apart from a low bicarbonate level.
senses.exampleCN: 除碳酸氢盐偏低外，她的生化指标都正常。
senses.why: Doctors compress 'the results of the biochemistry test' into the single word, another metonymy from discipline to output.
senses.whyCN: 医生把「生化检验的结果」压缩成一个词，这是又一次转喻：从学科名转向它的产出。

senses.title: Figurative inner workings
senses.definition: the hidden chemical or emotional workings of something, used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指某事物隐藏的化学或情感机制
senses.example: Popular science writes about the biochemistry of attraction.
senses.exampleCN: 科普写作会谈论吸引力的生化机制。
senses.why: Once the word means 'the chemistry behind a phenomenon', it can be borrowed for any hidden mechanism, especially in popular writing.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词表示「现象背后的化学」，它就能被借去指任何隐藏机制，在通俗写作中尤其常见。

intro.en: Biochemistry is a 19th-century compound of a Greek prefix for life and an English noun for chemistry, coined as the two sciences converged.
intro.cn: biochemistry 是 19 世纪的复合词，由表示生命的希腊语前缀与表示化学的英语名词构成，诞生于两门科学交汇之时。

items.en: bio- comes from Greek bios, 'life, course of life'. It became a scientific prefix in the 19th century, first in biology and then in a swarm of compounds.
items.cn: bio- 出自希腊语 bios「生命、生命历程」。它在 19 世纪成为科学前缀，先用于 biology，随后进入一大批复合词。

items.en: Chemistry reached English through alchemy, Medieval Latin alchimia and Arabic al-kimiya, usually traced to Greek khemeia. The earliest origin remains disputed, so the deeper etymology is uncertain.
items.cn: chemistry 经 alchemy、中世纪拉丁语 alchimia、阿拉伯语 al-kimiya 进入英语，通常追溯到希腊语 khemeia。更早的来源仍有争议，深层词源属于来源不确定。

items.en: The compound biochemistry is generally dated to the middle decades of the 19th century, when physiologists began to describe life in chemical terms. The exact coinage is not settled.
items.cn: biochemistry 这一复合词一般认为出现在 19 世纪中叶，当时生理学家开始用化学语言描述生命。确切的首创者尚无定论。

items.en: Around 1900 the field acquired its modern shape as enzymes, proteins and metabolic pathways were worked out, and university chairs followed.
items.cn: 约 1900 年，随着酶、蛋白质与代谢通路被阐明，这门学科获得现代形态，大学教席也随之设立。

items.en: In the 20th century hospitals created clinical biochemistry laboratories, adding the everyday sense of a set of test results.
items.cn: 20 世纪医院设立临床生化实验室，由此增加了「一组检验结果」这一日常义。

items.en: After the 1950s, biochemistry merged with molecular biology, and the word now covers both the classic chemistry of life and its molecular successor.
items.cn: 1950 年代以后，生物化学与分子生物学融合，这个词如今同时涵盖经典的生命化学与其分子层面的后继者。

note.en: The first group separates the noun from its adjective and from neighbouring life-science words; the second separates it from words for adjacent levels of study.
note.cn: 第一组把这个名词与它的形容词以及与相邻的生命科学词分开；第二组把它与邻近研究层次的词分开。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of the chemistry of life'; it describes tests, pathways and substances, while biochemistry names the field or the processes.
entries.definitionCN: 是形容词，意为「生命化学的」，用来修饰检验、通路、物质；biochemistry 则指学科或过程。

entries.definition: The study of living things in general, including their structure, growth and behaviour; it is wider than biochemistry.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指研究生物及其结构、生长与行为的学科，范围比生物化学更宽。

entries.definition: The person who practises biochemistry; the field itself never takes the -ist ending.
entries.definitionCN: 指从事生物化学的人；学科本身不能加 -ist 词尾。

entries.definition: The study of biological processes at the level of DNA, RNA and proteins; it overlaps heavily with biochemistry but centres on information flow.
entries.definitionCN: 在 DNA、RNA 与蛋白质层面研究生命过程，与生物化学高度重叠，但更侧重信息传递。

entries.definition: The study of how organs and tissues function; it asks what a body does, while biochemistry asks what reactions make it possible.
entries.definitionCN: 研究器官与组织如何运作，关心「身体做什么」；生物化学关心「哪些反应使之成为可能」。

entries.definition: The science of substances and their reactions in general; biochemistry is its living subset.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物质及其反应的一般科学；生物化学是它在生命领域的子集。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: bio- 'life' + chemistry: the chemistry of life.
normal.cn: bio-「生命」+ chemistry「化学」：生命的化学。

normal.en: The family runs biochemical, biochemist, biomolecule and metabolite.
normal.cn: 同族词有 biochemical、biochemist、biomolecule、metabolite。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: clinical biochemistry, biochemistry department, plant biochemistry.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：临床生物化学、生物化学系、植物生物化学。

normal.en: Hospitals say 'her biochemistry is normal' when they mean the lab panel.
normal.cn: 医院说「她的生化正常」，指的是一组化验指标。

normal.en: The word names both the field and the thing the field studies, like 'history' naming both a discipline and a past.
normal.cn: 这个词既指学科，也指学科研究的对象，就像 history 既指历史学也指过去。

abstract.en: Think of a city's traffic map: biochemistry is the map of every chemical route inside a cell.
abstract.cn: 想象一张城市交通图：生物化学就是细胞内每条化学反应路线的地图。

abstract.en: A biochemistry panel is a weather report for the body's internal climate.
abstract.cn: 一组生化指标就像身体内部气候的天气预报。

abstract.en: Picture a workshop where every tool is a molecule and every worker is an enzyme.
abstract.cn: 想象一间作坊：每件工具都是分子，每个工人都是酶。

examples.en: Biochemistry explains how cells extract energy from sugar.
examples.cn: 生物化学解释了细胞如何从糖中获取能量。

examples.en: She chose biochemistry because she wanted to understand life at the molecular level.
examples.cn: 她选择生物化学，是因为想在分子层面理解生命。

examples.en: The hospital's biochemistry laboratory reports results within an hour.
examples.cn: 医院的生化实验室一小时内出结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「bio（生命）+ chemistry（化学）」→ 研究生命里的化学 → 生物化学

root: 希腊语 bios「生命」+ chemistry（经阿拉伯语 al-kimiya、中世纪拉丁语 alchimia 上溯至希腊语 khemeia「冶金术」），19 世纪合成为 biochemistry。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from the discipline to its object, then to its composition, its teaching, its institutions, its clinical branch, its results and finally to figurative inner workings.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从学科移向研究对象，再到化学组成、课程、机构、临床分支、检验结果，最后落到比喻性的内在机制。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a list of molecular reactions extracted from a living cell.
core.cn: 核心意象：从一只活细胞里抽出来的一张分子反应清单。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE AND ITS OBJECT: the field itself, and the processes it studies.
branches.cn: 学科与其对象：这门学问本身，以及它所研究的那些过程。

branches.en: SUBSTANCE: what the cell contains rather than what it does.
branches.cn: 物质：细胞里有什么，而不是它做了什么。

branches.en: INSTITUTION: the subject as taught, and the department or laboratory that practises it.
branches.cn: 机构：作为科目的课程，以及从事该学科的院系或实验室。

branches.en: SPECIALISED ROUTES: a clinical branch and the chemistry of one named pathway.
branches.cn: 专门路线：一个临床分支，以及某条被点名的通路的化学。

branches.en: OUTPUT AND METAPHOR: the reported results, and the hidden chemistry of any phenomenon.
branches.cn: 产出与比喻：报告出来的结果，以及任何现象背后隐藏的化学。

intro.en: Biochemistry is a two-root compound with a Greek prefix and an English noun, plus the abstract suffix -istry.
intro.cn: biochemistry 是双词根复合词：希腊语前缀加英语名词，再带抽象名词后缀 -istry。

latinIntro.en: Greek supplies the element for life; the chemistry element came through Arabic and Medieval Latin. The suffix -istry descends from Latin -ia and Greek -ia.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语提供表示生命的成分；表示化学的成分经阿拉伯语与中世纪拉丁语传入；后缀 -istry 源自拉丁语 -ia 与希腊语 -ia。

items.example: Biochemistry became a separate degree in the twentieth century.
items.exampleCN: 生物化学在 20 世纪成为独立学位。

items.meaning: relating to the chemistry of life
items.example: The biochemical assay took two hours.
items.exampleCN: 这项生化测定用了两小时。

items.meaning: one who studies the chemistry of life
items.example: The biochemist grew crystals of the enzyme.
items.exampleCN: 这位生物化学家培养了该酶的晶体。

items.example: Biology and biochemistry share their first element.
items.exampleCN: 生物学与生物化学共享第一个构词成分。

items.meaning: a molecule produced by or belonging to life
items.meaningCN: 由生命产生或属于生命的分子
items.example: Proteins are the most versatile biomolecules.
items.exampleCN: 蛋白质是最多才多艺的生物分子。

items.example: The drug's main metabolite is inactive.
items.exampleCN: 该药物的主要代谢产物没有活性。

items.meaning: a protein that catalyses a reaction
items.example: Each step of the pathway needs its own enzyme.
items.exampleCN: 通路的每一步都需要各自的酶。

items.meaning: the science of substances and reactions
items.meaningCN: 研究物质与反应的科学
items.example: Chemistry provides the methods biochemistry uses.
items.exampleCN: 化学提供了生物化学所用的方法。

items.meaning: relating to the treatment of patients
items.example: Clinical biochemistry reports potassium levels.
items.exampleCN: 临床生物化学报告血钾水平。

definition_zh: adj. 野蛮的；残暴的；未开化的、粗鄙的；（古义）异族的、非希腊罗马的
definition_en: brutally cruel; uncivilised or crude in taste; in older use, of foreign peoples outside the Greek and Roman world
core_image: 卷宗里那种不该属于任何世纪的刑罚
scene: 法官读完卷宗，说这种刑罚不该出现在任何时代。 The judge closed the file and called the punishment barbaric, whatever the century.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：barbaric 指残暴野蛮；句意是法官合上卷宗，称这种刑罚无论放在哪个世纪都属于野蛮。

pos.zh: 野蛮的；残暴的；粗鄙的

forms.label: 形容词原级（比较级用 more）

senses.title: Brutally cruel
senses.definition: shockingly cruel and without any restraint of civilised feeling
senses.definitionCN: 残酷得令人震惊，毫无文明情感的约束
senses.example: The court described the treatment as barbaric.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭称这种对待方式是残暴的。
senses.why: The word moved from naming difference to naming cruelty, so it now judges the act rather than the origin of the actor.
senses.whyCN: 该词由「指认差异」转为「指认残暴」，因此如今评判的是行为，而非行为者的出身。

senses.title: Uncivilised or crude
senses.definition: lacking refinement in manners, art, or taste
senses.definitionCN: 在举止、艺术或趣味上缺乏教养与打磨
senses.example: The hall was decorated with barbaric splendour.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅装饰得奢华而粗野。
senses.why: Here the judgement is about polish rather than pain: too much gold, too little restraint.
senses.whyCN: 这里的评判关乎「打磨」而非「痛苦」：金子太多，克制太少。

senses.title: Foreign, in old use
senses.definition: in older writing, belonging to peoples outside the Greek and Roman world
senses.definitionCN: 旧时文献中指希腊罗马世界之外的族群
senses.example: The chronicler wrote of barbaric tribes beyond the river.
senses.exampleCN: 编年史家写到河外的异族部落。
senses.why: This is the original Greek sense: the word first imitated speech that sounded like bar bar to Greek ears.
senses.whyCN: 这是希腊语的原义：该词最初模仿在希腊人耳中听起来像「bar bar」的话语。

intro.en: Barbaric began as an imitation of unintelligible speech: bar bar. Greek turned that sound into a word for foreign, and history turned foreign into cruel.
intro.cn: barbaric 起初是对听不懂的话语的模仿：bar bar。希腊人把这个声音变成「异族」一词，历史又把「异族」变成了「残暴」。

items.en: Greek barbaros imitates speech that sounds like bar bar, so it first meant foreign.
items.cn: 希腊语 barbaros 模仿听起来像「bar bar」的话语，初义为「异族的」。

items.en: Greek barbarikos turns the noun into an adjective, of or like foreigners.
items.cn: 希腊语 barbarikos 把名词变为形容词，意为「异族的、像异族的」。

items.en: Latin barbaricus keeps the adjective for peoples outside the empire.
items.cn: 拉丁语 barbaricus 保留该形容词，指帝国之外的族群。

items.en: English takes the word through French, still mainly meaning foreign and unpolished.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入该词，仍主要表示「异族的、未加雕琢的」。

items.en: Wars and travel writing push the word toward savage cruelty rather than mere difference.
items.cn: 战争与游记把词义推向残暴，而不再只是「不同」。

items.en: Modern use splits: barbaric marks cruelty, barbarous marks crude taste, barbarian names the person.
items.cn: 现代用法分化：barbaric 指残暴，barbarous 偏粗鄙，barbarian 指其人。

note.en: The look-alike group first separates the three barbar- relatives by what each one names, then adds two false friends; the near-meaning group grades cruelty from wild to unrefined.
note.cn: 形近组先把三个 barbar- 亲属按各自所指区分开，再加入两个假朋友；近义组把「残酷」由凶猛到粗鄙分级排列。

entries.definition: Rough and unrefined, also cruel.
entries.definitionCN: 粗鄙未开化的，也可指残暴。

entries.definition: A member of a people thought uncivilised.
entries.definitionCN: 被视为未开化族群的一员。

entries.definition: Someone who cuts hair and trims beards.
entries.definitionCN: 理发修面的人。

entries.definition: A drug that depresses the nervous system.
entries.definitionCN: 抑制神经系统的药物。

entries.definition: Violently wild and uncontrolled.
entries.definitionCN: 凶猛不驯的。

entries.definition: Showing no mercy or feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 毫无怜悯的。

entries.definition: Willing to cause suffering.
entries.definitionCN: 乐于造成痛苦的。

entries.definition: Without the manners of an ordered society.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏有序社会礼教的。

normalIntro.en: Say bar bar aloud: that is what foreign speech sounded like to Greek ears, and barbaric is built on that stammer.
normalIntro.cn: 把 bar bar 念出声：这就是希腊人耳中异族语言的声音，而 barbaric 就建在这个「口吃」之上。

normal.en: Barbar- is the stammer, -ic is the adjective ending.
normal.cn: barbar- 是那个口吃声，-ic 是形容词词尾。

normal.en: Barbarian is the person; barbaric is the quality.
normal.cn: barbarian 指人，barbaric 指性质。

normal.en: Barbarity is the cruel act; barbarism is the crude state.
normal.cn: barbarity 指暴行，barbarism 指粗野状态。

normal.en: Barbaric has no -er form; use more barbaric.
normal.cn: barbaric 没有 -er 形式，比较级用 more barbaric。

normal.en: Barbaric splendour means rich but tasteless.
normal.cn: barbaric splendour 意为奢华却无品味。

abstract.en: A sound of not understanding, hardened into a verdict.
abstract.cn: 一声「听不懂」，硬化成了一句判词。

abstract.en: The moment difference is renamed as fault.
abstract.cn: 「不同」被改名为「过错」的那一刻。

abstract.en: Gold piled where restraint should stand.
abstract.cn: 本该站着克制的地方，堆满了金子。

examples.en: They condemned the barbaric treatment of prisoners.
examples.cn: 他们谴责对囚犯的残暴对待。

examples.en: The palace was a barbaric display of gold and mirrors.
examples.cn: 那座宫殿是金饰与镜子的粗野炫耀。

examples.en: More barbaric punishments were abolished that year.
examples.cn: 那一年废除了更野蛮的刑罚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「巴巴里克」——听不清的「巴巴」声就是词根 barbar-，加 -ic 成形容词。记一条线：bar bar 听不懂 → 异族 → 未开化 → 残暴。人叫 barbarian，性质叫 barbaric。

root: 希腊语 barbaros 模仿异族语言「bar bar」之声，初义「非希腊的、异族的」；派生 barbarikos，经拉丁语 barbaricus、法语进入英语，约 1400 年作 barbaric。17 世纪战争与游记把词义推向残暴，现代与 barbarous「粗鄙」、barbarian「其人」分工。

sensesIntro.en: Read the three senses as a history: first foreign, then unpolished, finally cruel. The order of the senses is the order of the prejudice.
sensesIntro.cn: 把三个义项当成一段历史来读：先是异族，再是无教养，最后是残暴。义项的顺序就是偏见形成的顺序。

definition_en: a government formed by two or more parties that agree on a shared programme and divide the cabinet posts between them

senses.title: Parties agree to govern as one
senses.titleCN: 两个以上政党签约共同执政
senses.definition: the cabinet that results when two or more parties sign a common programme and divide the ministerial posts between them
senses.definitionCN: 两个以上政党签署共同纲领、分配部长职位之后形成的内阁
senses.example: After weeks of bargaining, the two parties announced a coalition government.
senses.exampleCN: 经过数周讨价还价，两党宣布组成联合政府。
senses.why: The Latin source means 'grow together': separate parties, like separate shoots, fuse into one body at the negotiating table.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为「长到一起」：原本分开的政党像分开的枝条，在谈判桌边合成一个整体。

senses.title: The cabinet as a working body
senses.titleCN: 作为运转班子的联合内阁本身
senses.definition: the group of ministers drawn from the partner parties, considered as one body with its own meetings, papers and staff
senses.definitionCN: 由各伙伴党派抽调部长组成的班子，作为有会议、文件与班底的单一机构来看待
senses.example: The coalition government held its first cabinet meeting on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 联合内阁在周一召开了第一次内阁会议。
senses.why: Once the bargain is signed, the arrangement turns into an institution: the phrase stops naming the deal and starts naming the people who meet each week.
senses.whyCN: 协议签署之后，这个安排就变成机构：此时这个短语不再指那笔交易，而指每周开会的那批人。

senses.title: The term served under such a cabinet
senses.definition: the stretch of time from the swearing-in to the break-up during which the partners govern together
senses.definitionCN: 从宣誓就职到合作破裂之间、各党共同执政的那段时间
senses.example: That coalition government survived only fourteen months.
senses.exampleCN: 那一届联合政府只维持了十四个月。
senses.why: A cabinet is an event with a beginning and an end, so the same phrase can name the whole span rather than the body.
senses.whyCN: 一届内阁是有始有终的事件，因此同一个短语也能指整段时间，而不只是那个班子。

senses.title: A partnership with a majority
senses.titleCN: 席位过半、无需外援即可立法的联合政府
senses.definition: a partnership whose combined seats pass half the chamber, so it can legislate without help from outside parties
senses.definitionCN: 各党席位相加超过议会半数，无需外部政党支持即可立法的联合政府
senses.example: The two centre parties had enough seats for a majority coalition government.
senses.exampleCN: 两个中间派政党的席位足以组成多数联合政府。
senses.why: Seat arithmetic decides how strong the fusion is: a majority turns the partnership into a self-sufficient machine.
senses.whyCN: 席位算术决定这种合并有多结实：席位过半就把伙伴关系变成一台自足的机器。

senses.title: A partnership living on outside votes
senses.titleCN: 未过半、靠外部支持维持的少数联合政府
senses.definition: a partnership that holds office without half the seats, relying on the votes of parties outside the cabinet
senses.definitionCN: 席位不到半数、依靠内阁之外政党的投票维持执政的联合政府
senses.example: A minority coalition government must negotiate every budget with independents.
senses.exampleCN: 少数联合政府每份预算都得与独立议员协商。
senses.why: Growing together without a majority leaves the seam visible: every bill tests whether the partners can still hold hands.
senses.whyCN: 没有过半就合到一起，接缝始终露在外面：每一份法案都在检验伙伴们还能不能继续牵手。

senses.title: A grand bargain between the big rivals
senses.titleCN: 两大对手政党合组的大联合政府
senses.definition: an arrangement in which the two largest rival parties, normally opponents, share the cabinet during a crisis
senses.definitionCN: 通常在危机时期由两个最大的对立政党分享内阁的安排
senses.example: A grand coalition government was the only way out of the deadlock.
senses.exampleCN: 大联合政府是走出僵局的唯一办法。
senses.why: The fusion is most surprising when the partners were enemies: the phrase keeps its literal force, two things made one.
senses.whyCN: 当伙伴原本是敌人时，这种合并最出人意料：这个短语仍保留字面力量——两样东西变成一样。

senses.title: A stopgap cabinet
senses.titleCN: 看守或过渡性的联合政府
senses.definition: a temporary partnership that keeps the state running until a fresh election or a lasting agreement
senses.definitionCN: 在新选举或持久协议达成之前维持国家运转的临时联合班子
senses.example: A caretaker coalition government supervised the ballot and then resigned.
senses.exampleCN: 看守联合政府主持了投票，随后辞职。
senses.why: If the parties cannot yet agree on a full term, they can still agree on a short one: fusion with an expiry date.
senses.whyCN: 如果各党暂时无法就完整任期达成一致，仍可就一个短任期达成一致：带到期日的合并。

senses.title: The same device at local level
senses.titleCN: 地方与地区层面的联合执政
senses.definition: the same arrangement in a city, region or devolved assembly, often used to keep a single rival party out of office
senses.definitionCN: 在市、地区或下放权力的议会中采用的同一安排，常用来把某个对手政党挡在执政位置之外
senses.example: At city hall a coalition government of two small groups replaced the long-ruling party.
senses.exampleCN: 在市政厅，两个小党派的联合政府取代了长期执政的党。
senses.why: The pattern is scale-free: wherever seats are counted and posts are divided, partners can grow together.
senses.whyCN: 这种模式不分尺度：只要席位需要清点、职位需要分配，伙伴们就能合到一起。

intro.en: The word starts in Latin as an image of things growing into one another. Its use for a cabinet is a modern political extension rather than part of the original meaning, and coalition ministries were already called by that name in the late eighteenth century.
intro.cn: 这个词在拉丁语里最初是「事物彼此长合」的画面。用它指内阁属于近代的政治延伸，并非原义；十八世纪晚期的联合内阁已被这样称呼。

items.en: Alere 'to nourish, to feed' gave alescere, a verb meaning to begin to grow; the same family lies behind adolescent and adult.
items.cn: 意为「滋养、喂养」的拉丁动词衍生出「开始生长」的动词；「青少年」与「成年人」这两个英语词也出自同一族。

items.en: Co- 'together' plus alescere 'begin to grow' made coalescere 'to grow together, to fuse'; its past participle coalitus is the base of the noun of union.
items.cn: 表示「共同」的前缀加「开始生长」，构成「长到一起、合而为一」的拉丁动词；其过去分词是「联合」这一名词的基础。

items.en: The noun coalitio, built on that participle, named a growing together or a league; English took the political sense through French coalition, where it had meant a league of powers.
items.cn: 由该分词构成的拉丁名词指「长合」或「同盟」；英语经法语借入这一政治用法，法语中它曾指列强之间的同盟。

items.en: In seventeenth and eighteenth century French, coalition meant a temporary league of states or parties formed against a common rival.
items.cn: 在十七、十八世纪的法语里，这个词指国家或党派为对付共同对手而结成的临时同盟。

items.en: British politics applied it to cabinets: the Fox-North ministry of 1783 was widely called a coalition, and the label stuck to any multi-party cabinet.
items.cn: 英国政治把它用到内阁上：一七八三年的福克斯与诺斯联合内阁被普遍称作联合政府，此后任何多党内阁都沿用这一称呼。

items.en: In the twentieth century the phrase widened to cover majority and minority coalitions, grand coalitions of rivals, caretaker cabinets and coalitions in devolved assemblies.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个短语扩展到涵盖多数与少数联合政府、由对手组成的大联合政府、看守内阁，以及下放权力议会中的联合执政。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds close to the headword, and only one of them shares its root; the second group names neighbouring arrangements that are not the same thing.
note.cn: 第一组在拼写或读音上与词条接近，其中只有一个与它同源；第二组是相邻但不等同的制度安排。

entries.definition: The noun for any union of groups; on its own it can be a campaign alliance, an electoral pact or a business bloc, with no cabinet involved.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何团体结成的联合体；单独使用时可以指竞选同盟、选举协议或商业联盟，并不涉及内阁。

entries.definition: The verb from which the noun comes: separate parts merge into one mass, as cells or ideas do. It never means to form a cabinet.
entries.definitionCN: 名词所由来的动词：分开的部分合并成一团，如细胞或想法；它从不表示组阁。

entries.definition: The process of merging, used in physics and linguistics; it names the fusing, not the resulting body.
entries.definitionCN: 合并的过程，用于物理学与语言学；它指合并本身，而非合并后的机构。

entries.definition: From a Latin verb meaning 'to bring together', but it means comparing texts or gathering pages, not a political union.
entries.definitionCN: 出自意为「带到一起」的拉丁动词，但指比对文本或整理书页，与政治联合无关。

entries.definition: A general agreement to work together, often between states or parties and often for one purpose only; it need not produce a cabinet.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指合作约定，常见于国家或政党之间，往往只为一件事，不必产生内阁。

entries.definition: The name used when most parties join a cabinet to face a war, a collapse or a transition; the emphasis is on ending division, not on seat arithmetic.
entries.definitionCN: 多数党派为应对战争、崩溃或过渡而加入内阁时用的名称；强调结束分裂，而非席位数。

entries.definition: A cabinet formed by a single party that lacks a majority and governs with outside support; only one party holds the posts.
entries.definitionCN: 由单一政党组成、席位不过半、靠外部支持执政的内阁；部长职位只由一个党占有。

entries.definition: A chamber where no party has a majority; it is the situation that makes coalitions necessary, not the cabinet itself.
entries.definitionCN: 没有任何政党过半的议会；它是促成联合政府的局面，而不是内阁本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin picture, the real word family and the real political phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁语画面、真实的同族词与真实的政治说法。

normal.en: Co- 'together' plus a root meaning 'grow': two parties growing into one trunk.
normal.cn: 表示「共同」的前缀加表示「生长」的词根：两个政党长成一根主干。

normal.en: The family runs coalition, coalesce, coalescence, coalitionist and coalitional.
normal.cn: 同族词包括表示联合的名词、表示合并的动词、表示合并过程的名词，以及联合派与联盟形容词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the trade: form a coalition government, a grand coalition government, a caretaker coalition government.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出这一行当：组成联合政府、大联合政府、看守联合政府。

normal.en: Historical anchor: the Fox-North ministry of 1783 was already called a coalition, long before the phrase became ordinary.
normal.cn: 历史锚点：一七八三年的福克斯与诺斯内阁已被称作联合政府，远早于这个短语变得平常。

normal.en: Arithmetic anchor: majority and minority coalitions differ by seats, grand coalitions by the size of the partners.
normal.cn: 算术锚点：多数与少数联合政府差在席位，大联合政府差在伙伴的体量。

abstract.en: Two chairs face away from each other until someone turns both toward one table.
abstract.cn: 两把椅子本来背对着，直到有人把它们一起转向同一张桌子。

abstract.en: A post list is circled in two colours of ink, and every name carries two signatures.
abstract.cn: 一张职位名单被两种颜色的墨水圈过，每个名字后面都有两个签名。

abstract.en: A borrowed car with two drivers: it moves, but both hands sit on the wheel.
abstract.cn: 一辆借来的车有两个司机：车能走，但方向盘上有两双手。

examples.en: The coalition government fell when the junior partner withdrew its ministers.
examples.cn: 小党撤回部长后，联合政府垮台了。

examples.en: Economists warned that a coalition government would struggle to pass a budget.
examples.cn: 经济学家警告说，联合政府将难以通过预算。

examples.en: She covered the coalition government for a regional paper.
examples.cn: 她为一家地区报纸报道这届联合政府。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「科阿利申·政府」——谐音「合力伸」：各党把力气合起来，伸到同一张桌子上办事 → 联合政府

root: 拉丁 coalescere「长到一起」= co-（共同）+ alescere「生长」，源自 alere「滋养」；名词经法语进入英语，政府义为十九世纪后的政治用法。短语后半出自拉丁 gubernare「掌舵」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one bargain: parties grow together, sign a programme, meet as a body, hold office for a term, and then vary by seats, by the size of the partners, by how long the deal lasts and by the level of government.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一笔交易展开：各党长到一起、签下纲领、作为班子开会、执政一个任期，随后再按席位多寡、伙伴体量、协议时长与政府层级分化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: separate parties grow into one cabinet, then hold office until the seam shows.
core.cn: 核心意象：分开的政党长成一个内阁，然后执政到接缝暴露。

branches.en: THE DEAL AND ITS WEAK FORM: a signed fusion, and the version that survives without half the seats.
branches.cn: 协议与弱势版本：签约合并，以及席位不到半数仍能存活的那种。

branches.en: BODY AND BIG TWO: a weekly cabinet meeting, and the crisis version built from the largest rivals.
branches.cn: 班子与两大党：每周开会的内阁，以及由最大对手在危机中搭成的那种。

branches.en: FULL TERM AND STOPGAP: a term that runs its course, and a term with an expiry date set by the next election.
branches.cn: 完整任期与过渡任期：走完全程的任期，以及把到期日定在下一次选举的任期。

branches.en: MAJORITY: seats beyond half make the partnership self-sufficient.
branches.cn: 多数：席位过半使伙伴关系自足。

branches.en: LOCAL: the same device in a council or devolved assembly, scaled down but identical in logic.
branches.cn: 地方层面：同一装置用于市议会或下放议会，规模缩小而逻辑相同。

intro.en: The phrase is a noun plus a noun, and both halves are built from Latin pieces that also form many other English words.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个名词合成，而两半都由拉丁语构件搭起，这些构件还构成许多别的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Coalescere supplies the first noun through its participle; gubernare supplies the second through French; the suffixes -ition and -ment turn actions into nouns.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词「长到一起」经其分词提供第一个名词；拉丁动词「掌舵」经法语提供第二个名词的动词；表示动作的名词后缀把动作变成名词。

items.example: The prefix binds two separate things into one act.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把分开的两样东西绑进同一个动作。

items.structure: co- + alescere (Latin root, 'to begin to grow')
items.meaningCN: 表示「生长、开始生长」的词根
items.example: The root pictures a shoot putting out new wood.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根画出新枝抽出新木的画面。

items.meaningCN: 表示「动作或其结果」的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix turns the act of fusing into a countable noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「合并」这一动作变成可数名词。

items.meaning: a union of parties or groups
items.meaningCN: 党派或团体结成的联合体
items.example: The coalition held together for a full term.
items.exampleCN: 这个联合体撑满了整个任期。

items.meaning: the body that runs a state
items.example: The government published its spending plans.

items.structure: govern (verb base, from Latin gubernare 'to steer')
items.example: Coalitions govern by compromise.
items.exampleCN: 联合政府靠妥协来治理。

items.meaning: result or means of an action
items.meaningCN: 表示「动作的结果或手段」的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix makes the act of steering into an institution.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「掌舵」的动作变成一种机构。

items.meaningCN: 主张多党联合执政的人
items.example: The coalitionist defended the deal to both party boards.
items.exampleCN: 这位联合派向两个党的执委会为这笔协议辩护。

items.example: Coalitional discipline held through the budget vote.
items.exampleCN: 联合体的纪律在预算表决中维持住了。

items.example: The governmental reshuffle followed the election.
items.exampleCN: 选举之后发生了政府改组。

items.example: An intergovernmental panel reviewed the plan.
items.exampleCN: 一个政府间小组审查了该计划。

definition_zh: 不能飞的（鸟）；无翅或翅退化的（昆虫）；家养后不再飞的禽类；演化中失去飞行能力的；比喻无法起步的
definition_en: lacking the ability to fly, whether because of anatomy, domestication, or evolutionary loss, and figuratively unable to get off the ground
core_image: 一只企鹅站在冰缘，鳍状的前肢垂在身侧，身后是它走不进去的天空
scene: 冰缘上，一群黑白相间的大鸟摇摇摆摆地朝繁殖群走去，它们的鳍肢只能划水，不能托起身体。 At the edge of the ice, the flightless birds shuffled inland toward their colony.
sceneCN: 这里 flightless 是「不能飞的」（第 1 个义项：身体结构上不具备飞行能力的鸟类）；句意为在冰缘，这些不能飞的鸟摇摇摆摆地朝内陆的繁殖群走去。

pos.zh: 不能飞的；无翅的；（昆虫）无飞行阶段的

derivatives.zh: 不能飞的状态；无飞行能力

senses.title: Birds That Cannot Fly
senses.definition: describing birds whose wings or flippers cannot lift them into the air
senses.definitionCN: 描述翅膀或鳍肢无法把身体托入空中的鸟类
senses.example: Penguins are flightless, but their flippers make them fast swimmers.
senses.exampleCN: 企鹅不能飞，但它们的鳍肢使它们成为游泳好手。
senses.why: flight names the capacity, and -less removes it; the word simply says the bird has no flight, without saying why.
senses.whyCN: flight 命名这种能力，-less 把它拿走；这个词只是说这种鸟没有飞行能力，并不解释原因。

senses.title: Insects Without Working Wings
senses.definition: used of insects that have no wings at all or only reduced, useless ones
senses.definitionCN: 用于完全没有翅膀、或只有退化无用翅膀的昆虫
senses.example: Many beetles living in caves are flightless and blind.
senses.exampleCN: 许多生活在洞穴里的甲虫既不能飞，也看不见。
senses.why: the suffix states an absence, so it applies to any insect that lacks the organ the noun presupposes.
senses.whyCN: 这个后缀表示的是一种缺失，因此可用来指任何缺少名词所预设之器官的昆虫。

senses.title: Domesticated Breeds That No Longer Fly
senses.titleCN: 家养后不再飞的禽类品种
senses.definition: used of farm breeds whose bodies have grown too heavy or too stubby to fly
senses.definitionCN: 用于因身体过重或翅膀过短而无法飞行的家养品种
senses.example: The farm keeps a flightless duck breed for its eggs.
senses.exampleCN: 这家农场养一种不会飞的鸭品种，取用它的蛋。
senses.why: domestication removes the need and then the ability, so the adjective marks a loss produced by husbandry rather than by nature.
senses.whyCN: 驯化先取消需要，再取消能力，形容词因此标记的是饲养造成的丧失，而非自然造成的。

senses.title: Flight Lost in Evolution
senses.titleCN: 演化中失去飞行能力的（岛屿鸟类）
senses.definition: used of species whose ancestors flew but whose isolated populations lost that ability
senses.definitionCN: 用于祖先会飞、但孤立种群后来失去这种能力的物种
senses.example: Island rails became flightless within a few thousand years.
senses.exampleCN: 岛屿上的秧鸡在几千年内就失去了飞行能力。
senses.why: on islands without predators, wings cost more than they earn, and the adjective records the outcome of that trade.
senses.whyCN: 在没有捕食者的岛上，翅膀的代价高于收益，这个形容词记录的正是这笔交易的结果。

senses.title: The Island Niche of Lost Flight
senses.titleCN: 岛屿生态中「不能飞」的生态位
senses.definition: the ecological role filled by species that give up flight on predator-free islands
senses.definitionCN: 在无捕食者岛屿上放弃飞行的物种所占据的生态角色
senses.example: Flightless grazers on remote islands often replace large herbivores.
senses.exampleCN: 偏远岛屿上不能飞的食草动物常替代大型植食者。
senses.why: the adjective becomes a niche label because the loss of flight reshapes how a species feeds and breeds.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词之所以成为生态位标签，是因为失去飞行会重塑一个物种取食与繁殖的方式。

senses.title: Figurative: Unable to Take Off
senses.titleCN: 比喻：无法起飞、被束缚的
senses.definition: figurative, describing a plan, career or person unable to get started or to move freely
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指计划、事业或人无法起步、无法自由行动
senses.example: The project was flightless from the start, short of funds and staff.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目从一开始就无法起飞，缺钱也缺人。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the core image intact: wings may exist, but nothing lifts, and the ground holds.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻完整保留了核心意象：翅膀也许在，但没有东西能把它托起，地面牢牢拉住。

senses.title: The Wingless Stage of an Insect
senses.titleCN: 昆虫的无翅阶段（若虫、工蚁）
senses.definition: used of a stage in an insect's life, or a caste, that never develops wings
senses.definitionCN: 用于昆虫一生中某个从不长出翅膀的阶段或品级
senses.example: Worker ants are a flightless caste within a winged species.
senses.exampleCN: 工蚁是一个会飞的物种内部不能飞的品级。
senses.why: the species may fly, yet the stage does not, and the adjective marks the stage rather than the whole animal.
senses.whyCN: 物种会飞，这个阶段却不会；形容词标记的是阶段，而不是整个动物。

senses.title: Not Involving Flight at All
senses.titleCN: 字面：无需飞行的（设备、训练语境）
senses.definition: used of equipment, drills or training that involve no flying at all
senses.definitionCN: 用于完全不涉及飞行的设备、演练或训练
senses.example: Ground crews practise on a flightless simulator before touching a real aircraft.
senses.exampleCN: 地勤人员在接触真机之前，先在不会飞的模拟器上练习。
senses.why: here the suffix negates the activity rather than a bird's anatomy, so the adjective simply means without any flying.
senses.whyCN: 这里的后缀否定的是活动本身，而不是鸟的身体构造，因此形容词只表示「不涉及任何飞行」。

intro.en: Flightless is an English compound: flight, from Old English flyht, plus -less, from Old English -lēas 'free from, lacking'. It names a body that lacks the flight the base word presupposes.
intro.cn: flightless 是一个英语复合词：flight（来自古英语 flyht）加 -less（古英语 -lēas「没有、免于」）。它命名的是一个缺少基词所预设之飞行能力的身体。

items.en: Flyht is the action noun from fleogan 'to fly' plus -t; it names both the act and the group that performs it.
items.cn: flyht 是由 fleogan「飞」加 -t 构成的动作名词，既指动作，也指做出该动作的群体。

items.en: Old English -lēas meant 'free from, without', and it already formed adjectives such as slǣplēas 'sleepless'.
items.cn: 古英语 -lēas 意为「没有、免于」，当时就已构成 slǣplēas「不眠的」一类形容词。

items.en: German -los and Dutch -loos are the same suffix, so the pattern is Germanic rather than borrowed from Latin.
items.cn: 德语 -los 与荷兰语 -loos 是同一后缀，可见这一构词模式属日耳曼语，而非从拉丁语借入。

items.en: The adjective appears in English only in the modern period, once natural history needed a plain word for birds that cannot fly.
items.cn: 这个形容词到近代英语才出现，是博物学需要一个朴素的说法来描述不会飞的鸟时造出来的。

items.en: The same construction yields harmless, sleepless, weightless and wingless, all built on a noun plus -less rather than on a Latin prefix.
items.cn: 同一构词法造出了 harmless、sleepless、weightless、wingless，全都建立在「名词 + -less」上，而不是拉丁前缀。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Germanic origin of -lēas is a reconstruction, and no firm first citation is available for the adjective flightless.
items.cn: 来源不确定：-lēas 在日耳曼语之前的来源属重构形式，形容词 flightless 也没有可靠的最早书证。

note.en: Group one holds the base word and the -less formations that look like it; group two holds adjectives that describe the same incapacity from other angles.
note.cn: 第一组是基词以及外形相似的 -less 构词；第二组是从别的角度描述同一种「不能飞」的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun from which flightless is built; it names the capacity itself, while the -less form names its absence.
entries.definitionCN: flightless 所由构成的基词；它命名能力本身，而 -less 形式命名的是能力的缺失。

entries.definition: Flight plus -y 'given to', meaning fickle; the suffix adds a habit rather than removing a capacity, so the sense runs the other way.
entries.definitionCN: flight 加 -y「倾向于」，意为轻浮善变；后缀添加的是一种习性而非移除一种能力，词义方向正好相反。

entries.definition: Built on sight plus -less; it shares only the suffix, since sight comes from Old English gesiht and has nothing to do with flying.
entries.definitionCN: 由 sight 加 -less 构成；只共用后缀，sight 来自古英语 gesiht，与飞行毫无关系。

entries.definition: Built on weight plus -less; the shape is identical but the base belongs to the weighing family, not the flying one.
entries.definitionCN: 由 weight 加 -less 构成；外形完全相同，但基词属于「称重」词族，而非「飞行」词族。

entries.definition: Lacking wings outright; it names the missing organ, while flightless names the missing ability, which may survive in a wingless body.
entries.definitionCN: 指根本没有翅膀；它命名缺失的器官，而 flightless 命名缺失的能力，后者在没有翅膀的身体上也可能谈得上。

entries.definition: Kept from flying by an outside order or circumstance, as a grounded aircraft; the incapacity is temporary and imposed.
entries.definitionCN: 因外部命令或情况被禁止飞行，如停飞的飞机；这种不能飞是暂时的、外加的。

entries.definition: Confined to the ground by nature or circumstance; it is broader and more literary than flightless.
entries.definitionCN: 因天性或处境被限制在地面；比 flightless 更宽泛，也更有文学色彩。

entries.definition: A neutral technical negative used of species or stages that do not fly; it states the fact without implying loss.
entries.definitionCN: 中性的技术性否定词，用于不飞的物种或阶段；只陈述事实，不含「丧失」之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the base word, the real suffix and the real parallel formations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：基词、真实后缀与真实平行构词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: flight + -less: the suffix takes away exactly what the noun supplies.
normal.cn: flight + -less：后缀拿走的正是名词提供的那样东西。

normal.en: German -los and Dutch -loos prove the suffix is Germanic, not Latin.
normal.cn: 德语 -los 与荷兰语 -loos 证明这个后缀属日耳曼语，而非拉丁语。

normal.en: harmless, sleepless, weightless, wingless: one pattern, many nouns.
normal.cn: harmless、sleepless、weightless、wingless：一个模式，多个名词。

normal.en: Penguins are the standard example: flippers for swimming, nothing for lifting.
normal.cn: 企鹅是标准例子：鳍肢用来游泳，没有东西用来升空。

normal.en: On islands the word becomes an ecological label, because loss of flight changes how a species lives.
normal.cn: 在岛屿上这个词变成生态学标签，因为失去飞行会改变一个物种的生活方式。

abstract.en: Picture a kite with a perfect frame and no wind beneath it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只骨架完好、身下却没有风的风筝。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase whose top step ends at a locked door.
abstract.cn: 想象一道楼梯，最高一级尽头是一扇锁住的门。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of wings folded neatly and never opened again.
abstract.cn: 想象一对折得整整齐齐、再也不展开的翅膀。

examples.en: New Zealand once held dozens of flightless bird species.
examples.cn: 新西兰曾经有数十种不会飞的鸟类。

examples.en: The beetle's flightless females look almost like larvae.
examples.cn: 这种甲虫不能飞的雌性看起来几乎像幼虫。

examples.en: Without wind, the design remained flightless no matter how light it was.
examples.cn: 没有风，这个设计无论多轻都无法起飞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「弗莱特莱斯」——翅膀像被剪掉一样轻，却怎么也升不起来 → 不能飞的。

root: flight（古英语 flyht，fleogan「飞」+ -t）+ -less（古英语 -lēas「缺乏、没有」，与德语 -los、荷兰语 -loos 同源）；-lēas 更早的来源属重构形式，形容词本身首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all deny one capacity. The denial can come from anatomy, from a wingless stage, from breeding, from evolution on islands, from the niche that loss creates, from a metaphor about plans, or from a context where no flying is involved at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在否定同一种能力。这种否定可能来自身体构造、无翅阶段、人工饲养、岛屿演化、丧失所造就的生态位、关于计划的比喻，或来自一个根本不涉及飞行的语境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: wings present or absent, and the air never entered.
core.cn: 核心意象：翅膀也许在、也许不在，但那片天空始终没有被进入。

branches.en: ANATOMY: the bird or insect simply lacks the organ or the power.
branches.cn: 构造：鸟或昆虫干脆缺少器官或力量。

branches.en: LOSS BY CIRCUMSTANCE: breeding makes the body heavy, a caste or stage never grows wings.
branches.cn: 处境造成的丧失：饲养让身体变重，某个品级或阶段则从不长翅。

branches.en: EVOLUTION ON ISLANDS: flight is traded away and the loss becomes a way of life.
branches.cn: 岛屿演化：飞行被交换掉，丧失本身成了一种生活方式。

branches.en: METAPHOR: plans and people can also fail to lift off.
branches.cn: 比喻：计划和人同样可能升不起来。

branches.en: NO FLYING INVOLVED: the suffix can negate the activity, not the animal.
branches.cn: 不涉及飞行：后缀可以否定活动，而不是否定动物。

intro.en: Flightless is transparent: a Germanic noun for flying, plus a Germanic suffix of deprivation. The interest lies in how far that deprivation can be stretched.
intro.cn: flightless 的结构一目了然：一个表「飞」的日耳曼名词，加一个表「剥夺」的日耳曼后缀；值得玩味的是这种剥夺能被拉伸到多远。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entry applies here: both halves are Germanic, and the nearest Latin idea, 'without', is expressed by a different prefix entirely.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有适用的拉丁词形：两半都属日耳曼语，而拉丁语中「没有」这一概念完全由另一个前缀表达。

items.structure: fleogan (Old English strong verb, class II)
items.meaning: to move through the air on wings
items.example: The base verb names the capacity that will be denied.
items.exampleCN: 基词动词命名的是后来被否定的那种能力。

items.meaning: the act of doing the verb
items.example: Flight is the act, not the actor.
items.exampleCN: flight 指动作，不指施动者。

items.example: The noun must exist before it can be denied.
items.exampleCN: 名词必须先存在，才谈得上被否定。

items.example: The suffix turns a possession into an absence.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「拥有」变成「没有」。

items.example: The adjective is a plain statement of absence.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是对缺失的朴素陈述。

items.meaning: the state of being unable to fly
items.example: Flightlessness evolved repeatedly on isolated islands.
items.exampleCN: 不能飞的状态在孤立岛屿上反复演化出来。

items.meaning: in a manner that involves no flying
items.example: The adverb is rare and mostly technical.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词罕用，多见于技术文字。

items.example: Wingless names the organ, flightless names the power.
items.exampleCN: wingless 指器官，flightless 指能力。

items.example: The same suffix produced slǣplēas in Old English.
items.exampleCN: 同一后缀在古英语中造出了 slǣplēas。

items.meaning: the line along which a flying thing travels
items.example: A flightless bird has no flight path to record.
items.exampleCN: 不会飞的鸟没有飞行路线可记录。

definition_zh: 驯化；驯养；栽培化；使野生物种适应人类利用的过程
definition_en: the process by which wild animals or plants are brought under human control and use
core_image: 一只野禽在几代人的挑选下翅膀变短、产蛋变多，栏门从篱笆变成木门，最后变成一把锁
scene: 村口的羊圈里， Generations of selection have made domestication visible in the shorter horns of the flock.
sceneCN: 这里 domestication 指「把野生物种驯化为家养的过程」（第 1 个义项：动物驯化）；句意为数代选育使驯化的痕迹显现在羊群变短的角上。图中可辨识物件：羊圈木栏、短角羊、选留标记、饲料槽。

pos.zh: 驯化；驯养；栽培化（不可数）；一次驯化事件（可数）

senses.title: Bringing wild animals under human control
senses.titleCN: 把野生动物置于人的控制之下
senses.definition: the process by which a wild animal population is bred and managed by people
senses.definitionCN: 野生兽群被人类繁育与管理的过程
senses.example: Dog domestication began before farming, according to the burial evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 据墓葬证据，狗的驯化早于农耕。
senses.why: domestic comes from Latin domus 'house', so domestication is literally the process of bringing a wild thing into the household.
senses.whyCN: domestic 出自拉丁 domus「家」，因此驯化字面上就是把野物带进家户的过程。

senses.title: Turning a wild plant into a crop
senses.definition: the process by which a wild plant is selected and changed until it depends on cultivation
senses.definitionCN: 野生植物被选育改变，直到依赖栽培的过程
senses.example: Maize domestication reshaped the cob from a few hard seeds to a full ear.
senses.exampleCN: 玉米的驯化把几粒硬籽的穗轴改造成饱满的果穗。
senses.why: the household image extends to plants: a field is a household arrangement for a species that can no longer scatter its own seed.
senses.whyCN: 「家户」的意象扩展到植物：田是为一个再也不能自己散播种子的物种安排的家。

senses.title: The domesticated condition
senses.definition: the state of a species or individual that has become dependent on human care
senses.definitionCN: 某物种或个体已变得依赖人类照料的状态
senses.example: Domestication left the breed unable to survive without shelter.
senses.exampleCN: 驯化使这个品种离开人工庇护就无法生存。
senses.why: the process name also names its result, because a species that has been through it looks different from its wild relatives.
senses.whyCN: 过程名也指结果，因为经历过这一过程的物种与野生亲戚看起来不同。

senses.title: Making something wild feel familiar
senses.titleCN: 使野性之物变得可亲近
senses.definition: figuratively, the process of taming or civilising something that was once unfamiliar
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指把曾经陌生之物变得驯顺或文明化的过程
senses.example: The domestication of the forest into a park took a century.
senses.exampleCN: 把森林驯化成公园用了一个世纪。
senses.why: once the word means bringing inside, it can describe any wildness reduced to something a household can handle.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词表示「带进家里」，它就能描述任何被削减到家户可处理程度的野性。

senses.title: A shared set of changes in tame species
senses.titleCN: 家养物种共有的一组变化
senses.definition: the recurring package of traits, such as smaller horns and patchy coat, seen in many domesticated animals
senses.definitionCN: 许多家养动物身上反复出现的一组性状，如角变小、毛色出现斑块
senses.example: Floppy ears and shorter snouts are part of the domestication syndrome.
senses.exampleCN: 垂耳与较短的吻部是驯化综合征的一部分。
senses.why: breeding for calmness repeatedly pulled along other traits, so science gave the bundle a name built on domestication.
senses.whyCN: 为温顺而选育，反复连带出其他性状，科学于是给这束变化起了一个建于 domestication 上的名字。

senses.title: Reshaping a landscape
senses.titleCN: 把景观改造为人工环境
senses.definition: the long process by which people convert a wild landscape into one they manage
senses.definitionCN: 人们把野地改造成由自己管理的景观的长期过程
senses.example: Landscape domestication produced terraces, hedges and wells.
senses.exampleCN: 景观驯化造出了梯田、树篱与水井。
senses.why: if animals and plants can be brought inside, so can a whole valley, and the same word covers the slow reshaping.
senses.whyCN: 既然动植物能被带进家户，整座山谷也可以，同一个词覆盖这种缓慢改造。

senses.title: Making an idea or technology familiar
senses.titleCN: 使想法或技术变得日常可用
senses.definition: the process by which a novel idea or tool becomes ordinary and easy to use
senses.definitionCN: 新想法或新工具变得寻常、易用的过程
senses.example: The domestication of the telephone took two generations.
senses.exampleCN: 电话走进日常生活用了两代人。
senses.why: a new tool is wild in the sense that no one knows how to live with it; domestication is learning to live with it.
senses.whyCN: 新工具之所以「野」，是因为没人知道怎么与它共处；驯化就是学会与它共处。

senses.title: Bringing a treaty into domestic law
senses.definition: in law, the incorporation of an international agreement into a state's own legal system
senses.definitionCN: 法律上把国际协定纳入本国法律体系
senses.example: The domestication of the convention required a new statute.
senses.exampleCN: 该公约的国内法化需要一部新法规。
senses.why: legal writers reuse the household image: an international text must be brought inside the house of national law.
senses.whyCN: 法律写作者沿用「家户」意象：国际文本必须被带进国家法律这座房子。

intro.en: Domestication is built on Latin domesticus 'of the household', from domus 'house', with the English verb ending -ate and the noun ending -ion. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: domestication 建于拉丁 domesticus「属于家户的」之上，再上为 domus「房子」，加英语动词词尾 -ate 与名词词尾 -ion。年代均为约数。

items.en: Domus meant 'house, household'. Its pre-Latin base is reconstructed; the usual link to a root meaning 'to build' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: domus 意为「房子、家户」。它在拉丁语之前的词基属重构；通常把它联系到意为「建造」的词根，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Domesticus meant 'belonging to the household', applied to slaves, animals and things kept inside a house.
items.cn: domesticus 意为「属于家户的」，用于指奴隶、动物与养在屋内之物。

items.en: Domare 'to tame' is a separate verb with its own reconstructed root; it overlaps in meaning but should not be presented as the source of domesticus.
items.cn: domare「使驯服」是另一个动词，有自己的重构词根；它与 domesticus 意义重叠，却不应被说成 domesticus 的来源。

items.en: Domesticare meant 'to make domestic, to tame', and English took it as domesticate.
items.cn: domesticare 意为「使成为家用的、使驯服」，英语借作 domesticate。

items.en: English domestication appeared in the seventeenth century, first for taming animals and later for plants and landscapes.
items.cn: 英语 domestication 在 17 世纪出现，先指驯服动物，后扩及植物与景观。

items.en: In the twentieth century the noun became standard in archaeology and genetics, and law borrowed it for incorporating treaties; source uncertain for the first legal use.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个名词在考古学与遗传学中成为标准用语，法律也借用它指纳入条约；首次法律用法不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin household word; the second names other processes of bringing organisms or land under human use.
note.cn: 第一组共用拉丁「家户」词；第二组是把生物或土地纳入人类利用的其他过程。

entries.definition: Belonging to the home or to animals kept in it; it describes the state, not the historical process.
entries.definitionCN: 指属于家庭或养在家中的；描述状态，而非历史过程。

entries.definition: To bring a wild species under human use; the verb names the act, the noun names the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 指把野生物种纳入人类利用；动词指动作，名词指整套过程。

entries.definition: Already tamed or adapted; it looks back at a completed action rather than naming the action.
entries.definitionCN: 指已被驯化或适应；回看已完成的动作，而非命名动作。

entries.definition: The quality or state of home life; it has nothing to do with taming species.
entries.definitionCN: 指家庭生活的性质或状态；与驯化物种无关。

entries.definition: Making one animal calm and obedient to people; it can happen without any change in the species.
entries.definitionCN: 使单只动物变得温顺听话；可以完全不涉及物种层面的改变。

entries.definition: Preparing and working land to grow crops; it names the labour, not necessarily the genetic change.
entries.definitionCN: 指整地耕作以种作物；指劳动，不一定指遗传改变。

entries.definition: Adjustment of an organism to a new climate or habitat; no human household is implied.
entries.definitionCN: 生物对新气候或生境的适应；不隐含人类家户。

entries.definition: The founding of a permanent community in a place; it is about people staying, not species being tamed.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某地建立永久社区；说的是人定居，不是物种被驯化。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin house word, the family it built and the phrases archaeology keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁「房子」词、它构成的词族，以及考古学固定的搭配。

normal.en: domus 'house' + -ticus 'belonging to' + -ation 'process' = the process of bringing a wild thing into the house.
normal.cn: domus「房子」+ -ticus「属于」+ -ation「过程」= 把野物带进家户的过程。

normal.en: The family runs domestic, domesticate, domesticated, domestication and domesticity.
normal.cn: 词族包括 domestic、domesticate、domesticated、domestication、domesticity。

normal.en: Domare 'to tame' is a different Latin verb that happens to overlap in meaning.
normal.cn: domare「使驯服」是另一个拉丁动词，只是意义恰好重叠。

normal.en: The standard collocations are animal domestication, plant domestication and domestication syndrome.
normal.cn: 标准搭配是「动物驯化」「植物驯化」「驯化综合征」。

normal.en: The word is uncountable: a process, not a count of events.
normal.cn: 这个词不可数：指过程，而不计次数。

abstract.en: Picture a threshold that a species crosses once and cannot cross back.
abstract.cn: 想象一道门槛，一个物种跨过去一次，就再也跨不回来。

abstract.en: Picture a hand choosing seed from the calmest plant, year after year.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手年复一年从最安静的植株上留种。

abstract.en: Picture a wild valley drawn slowly into a floor plan.
abstract.cn: 想象一座野谷被缓慢画进一张平面图。

examples.en: The domestication of the horse changed transport across the steppe.
examples.cn: 马的驯化改变了草原上的运输方式。

examples.en: Genetic studies date wheat domestication to the Fertile Crescent.
examples.cn: 遗传研究把小麦的驯化定在肥沃新月地带。

examples.en: The report examines the domestication of international labour standards.
examples.cn: 这份报告考察国际劳工标准的国内法化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「多麦斯提凯申」听成「多麦斯（多把麦子）提进家」——把野麦一担担提进屋、年年留种，就是驯化。

root: 拉丁 domus「房子、家户」构成 domesticus「属于家户的」，再构成 domesticare「使驯服、使家用」，英语取其动词作 domesticate，加 -ion 成 domestication。domare「使驯服」是另一个动词，并非 domesticus 的来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from animal and plant domestication through the domesticated state, the figurative taming of anything wild, the trait bundle, landscape reshaping, familiar technology and legal incorporation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从动植物驯化，经被驯养状态、对任何野性的比喻性驯服、性状束、景观改造、技术日常化，到法律的国内法化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wild bird whose wings shorten generation by generation behind a gate.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只野禽在门后一代代地短了翅膀。

branches.en: ANIMALS AND PLANTS: selection behind a fence and selection in a field are one method aimed at two kingdoms.
branches.cn: 动物与植物：栏后的选育与田里的选育，是同一种方法指向两个界。

branches.en: STATE AND SYNDROME: the result of breeding is a dependent animal with a recognisable bundle of traits.
branches.cn: 状态与综合征：选育的结果是一只依赖人的动物，带着一组可辨认的性状。

branches.en: ANY WILDNESS: what is unfamiliar can be brought inside just as an animal is.
branches.cn: 任何野性：陌生之物也可以像动物一样被带进家户。

branches.en: LAND: a whole valley can be domesticated into terraces, hedges and wells.
branches.cn: 土地：整座山谷可以被驯化成梯田、树篱与水井。

branches.en: TOOLS AND TREATIES: a telephone and an international convention are both brought inside a house of use or law.
branches.cn: 工具与条约：电话与国际公约都被带进「使用」或「法律」这座房子。

intro.en: Domestication is a Latin household adjective turned into a verb and then into a noun of process.
intro.cn: domestication 是一个拉丁「家户」形容词，先变动词，再变表示过程的名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin domus also gives domicile and domestic, while domare 'to tame' is a separate verb whose similarity is semantic rather than etymological.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 domus 还给出 domicile 与 domestic；domare「使驯服」是另一个动词，其相似是语义上的，而非词源上的。

items.example: The stem supplies the image of bringing something indoors.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干提供「把某物带进屋内」的意象。

items.example: The ending makes domesticus 'of the household'.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾构成 domesticus「属于家户的」。

items.example: The ending turns domestic into domesticate.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾把 domestic 变成 domesticate。

items.example: The ending turns the verb into a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾把动词变成过程名词。

items.meaning: of the home; kept at home
items.example: Domestic animals depend on people.
People domesticated goats early.
items.exampleCN: 人们很早就驯化了山羊。

items.example: The domesticated form has smaller seeds.
Domestication took many generations.
The novel praises domesticity.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说赞美家庭生活。

derivatives.meaning: a second taming of a feral population
derivatives.meaningCN: 对野化群体的再次驯化

definition_zh: 在一定程度上；部分地（表示某说法只部分成立，留有保留）
definition_en: partly; in some measure, but not completely
core_image: 一杯水只倒到杯身一半，杯口还空着一截
scene: 老师看完两份实验记录，指出其中一份的结论只说对了一半。 The first explanation holds to a certain extent, but it ignores the second cause.
sceneCN: 这里取「在一定程度上」（第 1 个义项：限定说法成立的比例）；句意为第一种解释在一定程度上成立，但忽略了第二个原因。

pos.zh: 介词短语：在一定程度上；部分地

collocations.phrase: to a certain extent dependent on

senses.title: Partly true
senses.titleCN: 部分成立义：只对一部分
senses.definition: used to limit the strength of a statement so that it claims only partial truth
senses.definitionCN: 用来限定陈述的力度，只主张部分成立
senses.example: The model fits the observations to a certain extent.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型在一定程度上符合观测。
senses.why: Extent is a stretch, and a stretch can stop before it covers the whole distance.
senses.whyCN: 程度本是一段伸展，而伸展可以在走完全程之前停住。

senses.title: Beside the plain twin
senses.titleCN: 近义辨析：与另一变体的量差
senses.definition: it suggests a limited but definite measure, while the shorter twin is vaguer about how much
senses.definitionCN: 它暗示有限但确定的分量，而较短的近义说法对分量更含糊
senses.example: Costs fell to a certain extent, though not as much as promised.
senses.exampleCN: 成本有一定程度下降，但没有承诺的那么多。
senses.why: Adding the article makes the measure sound counted rather than waved away.
senses.whyCN: 加上冠词让这个分量听起来是被计过的，而不是随手一挥。

senses.title: On a scale of degree
senses.titleCN: 梯度义：与更大程度说法对照
senses.definition: it sits low on a scale that runs from a limited degree through a large degree to the whole
senses.definitionCN: 它处在一条由小程度经大程度到全体的尺度上的低处
senses.example: To a certain extent, the two explanations overlap.
senses.exampleCN: 在一定程度上，两种解释有重叠。
senses.why: Degree words form a ladder, and this rung is deliberately low.
senses.whyCN: 表程度的词构成一架梯子，这一级故意放得很低。

senses.title: Modifying an adjective
senses.titleCN: 修饰义：直接限定形容词
senses.definition: it can qualify an adjective or a verb, softening an assessment without denying it
senses.definitionCN: 可限定形容词或动词，软化评价而不否认它
senses.example: The report is reliable to a certain extent.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告在一定程度上可靠。
senses.why: A measure phrase at the end of a clause works like a dimmer switch on the judgement.
senses.whyCN: 句末的表量短语像调光开关，把判断调暗一些。

senses.title: A concessive move
senses.titleCN: 让步义：先退一步再补充
senses.definition: in argument it concedes a point partially before the speaker adds a reservation
senses.definitionCN: 在论证中先部分承认对方观点，随后再补上保留
senses.example: I accept the criticism to a certain extent.
senses.exampleCN: 我在一定程度上接受这一批评。
senses.why: Concession needs a stopper, and the limited measure stops the admission from becoming total.
senses.whyCN: 让步需要一个限位器，有限的分量正好防止承认变成全盘接受。

senses.title: Not a spatial range
senses.definition: it measures how far a statement holds, not how far a place or an area reaches
senses.definitionCN: 它量的是说法成立的程度，而非某地或某区域延伸的范围
senses.example: The outcome depends to a certain extent on decisions made elsewhere.
senses.exampleCN: 结果在一定程度上取决于别处作出的决定。
senses.why: The noun has a physical sense of area, but this phrase uses only the abstract sense of degree.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词有具体面积的义，但这个短语只用抽象的程度义。

senses.title: A hedge in research
senses.definition: in academic writing it keeps a conclusion from claiming more than the evidence supports
senses.definitionCN: 在学术写作中，避免结论超出证据所能支撑的范围
senses.example: The finding supports the hypothesis to a certain extent.
senses.exampleCN: 这一发现一定程度上支持该假设。
senses.why: Scholarship rewards caution, and a stated limit is a mark of care rather than weakness.
senses.whyCN: 学术看重谨慎，写明限度是细致的表现而非软弱。

senses.title: A hedge in promises
senses.definition: in everyday talk it warns that a benefit or a repair will only go part of the way
senses.definitionCN: 在日常谈话中，提醒某项好处或修理只能起到部分作用
senses.example: The medicine will ease the pain to a certain extent.
senses.exampleCN: 这药会在一定程度上减轻疼痛。
senses.why: Promises sound safer when a limit is named, which is why the phrase appears in advice.
senses.whyCN: 写明限度会让承诺听起来更稳妥，因此这个短语常出现在叮嘱里。

intro.en: Extent comes from Latin extentus, the participle of extendere, to stretch out, built on tendere, to stretch. Certain comes from Latin certus, settled or sure. Both sources are secure; the phrase is modern.
intro.cn: extent 来自拉丁语 extentus，是 extendere「向外伸展」的分词，其下为 tendere「拉」。certain 来自拉丁语 certus「已定的、确然的」。两处来源都清楚；短语属近代。

items.en: Tendere meant to stretch or pull, and it supplies a large family of English tension words.
items.cn: tendere 意为拉伸、牵引，构成英语中一大批表张力的词。

items.en: The prefix for out plus the verb gave the sense of stretching something out to its full length.
items.cn: 表向外的前缀加动词，给出把某物拉伸到全长的意思。

items.en: The participle became a noun for the distance covered, hence range and degree.
items.cn: 分词转为名词，指所覆盖的距离，由此有范围与程度。

items.en: Certus meant settled or decided, and English certain keeps both the sure and the unspecified senses.
items.cn: certus 意为已定、已决，英语 certain 兼留确然与某一未指明两种义。

items.en: The hedging frame belongs to modern written argument; first dates are approximate.
items.cn: 这个限定框架属于近代书面论证，首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group varies the measure or the degree; the second group are one-word hedges with the same caution.
note.cn: 第一组替换分量或程度；第二组是同属谨慎语气的单词限定语。

entries.definition: It limits a claim without suggesting a counted degree.
entries.definitionCN: 限定主张，但不暗示被计过的分量。

entries.definition: It concedes most of the claim, which is nearly the opposite force.
entries.definitionCN: 承认主张的大部分，力度几乎相反。

entries.definition: It sounds more conversational and slightly less precise.
entries.definitionCN: 更口语，也略欠精确。

entries.definition: It refers to a measure already named earlier in the text.
entries.definitionCN: 回指上文已经提到的分量。

entries.definition: A single adverb for a partial claim.
entries.definitionCN: 单个副词表部分成立。

entries.definition: It softens an adjective rather than measuring a claim.
entries.definitionCN: 用来软化形容词，而非给主张量度。

entries.definition: It often divides a whole into contributing parts.
entries.definitionCN: 常把整体分成若干起作用的部分。

entries.definition: It grants a claim only as far as a stated point.
entries.definitionCN: 只承认到某一明确限度为止。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real stretching root, the settled sense of certain, and the real hedging grammar of degree.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实的拉伸词根、已定的限定词，以及真实的程度限定语法。

normal.en: Extent is a stretch, so a claim can stretch only part of the way.
normal.cn: 程度是一段伸展，因此主张只能伸展到半途。

normal.en: Certain here means a fixed but unnamed measure, not a sure fact.
normal.cn: 此处的限定词指固定但未指明的分量，不是确然的事实。

normal.en: It sits low on a degree ladder that runs up to a large extent.
normal.cn: 它位于一架通往大程度的梯子的低处。

normal.en: At the end of a clause it works like a dimmer on the judgement.
normal.cn: 放在句末时，它像给判断装了调光器。

normal.en: It concedes a point without surrendering the argument.
normal.cn: 它让出一小步，却不交出整个论点。

abstract.en: Like a glass filled halfway, with the top half still empty.
abstract.cn: 像只倒了一半的杯子，上半截还空着。

abstract.en: Like a door opened a crack: enough to see through, not enough to walk in.
abstract.cn: 像门只开一条缝：够看见里面，不够走进去。

abstract.en: Like a dimmer turned low, so the light shows the room without flooding it.
abstract.cn: 像把调光器调低，照见房间却不至于晃眼。

examples.en: The two accounts agree to a certain extent.
examples.cn: 两种说法在一定程度上是一致的。

examples.en: Her prediction was right to a certain extent.
examples.cn: 她的预测在一定程度上是对的。

examples.en: The plan depends to a certain extent on the weather.
examples.cn: 这个计划在一定程度上要看天气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「图 阿 瑟顿 伊克斯滕特」——杯子只倒了一半，杯口还空着：在一定程度上

root: 核心名词意为程度，来自拉丁语 extentus「伸展」，出自动词 extendere「向外拉伸」；限定词出自拉丁语 certus「已定的」。该短语为近代书面语定型，首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses separate partial truth, the contrast with the vaguer twin, the place on a degree ladder, adjectival modification, concession, the exclusion of spatial range, academic hedging and everyday promises.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项区分：部分成立、与含糊近义说的对照、在程度梯度上的位置、修饰形容词、让步、排除空间范围、学术限定、日常承诺留余地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass filled exactly halfway, the upper half still empty.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只只倒到一半的杯子，上半截仍空着。

branches.en: THE PART: a claim is granted only as far as the measure reaches.
branches.cn: 部分：主张只在分量所及之处被承认。

branches.en: THE SCALE: the same frame varies from a small to a large degree.
branches.cn: 尺度：同一框架从小分量一直排到大分量。

branches.en: THE MODIFIER: an adjective or a verb is softened rather than denied.
branches.cn: 修饰：形容词或动词被软化，而不是被否定。

branches.en: THE LIMIT: degree is meant, not the area a place covers.
branches.cn: 边界：说的是程度，不是某地覆盖的面积。

branches.en: THE REGISTER: research and advice both use the limit to stay honest.
branches.cn: 语域：研究与叮嘱都用限度来保持诚实。

intro.en: The phrase combines a Latin noun of stretching with a Latin adjective of settled measure.
intro.cn: 这个短语把一个表伸展的拉丁语名词与一个表既定分量的拉丁语形容词结合在一起。

latinIntro.en: The noun comes from extendere, to stretch out, on tendere, to stretch; the limiting word comes from certus, settled.
latinIntro.cn: 名词出自 extendere「向外拉伸」，其下为 tendere「拉」；限定词出自 certus「已定的」。

items.example: The verb is the base of tension and extension alike.
items.exampleCN: 这个词是张力与延伸两族词的根。

items.example: The prefix adds direction away from the centre.
items.exampleCN: 前缀加上离开中心的方向。

items.example: The participle turned into a noun of range.
items.exampleCN: 分词转为表范围的名词。

items.example: English keeps the abstract measure and the physical area.
items.exampleCN: 英语兼留抽象程度与具体面积。

items.example: The verb restores the action behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词恢复了名词背后的动作。

items.example: The adjective describes wide coverage.
The noun names the result of stretching.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指拉伸的结果。

items.example: The adjective yields the limiting word in the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词给出短语中的限定词。

items.example: The frame is a standard hedge in argument.
items.exampleCN: 这个框架是论证中的标准限定语。

definition_zh: 礼仪；得体；端庄；合乎场合的举止
definition_en: correct and dignified behaviour that suits the occasion and shows self-control
core_image: 葬礼上所有人压低声音，手机收进口袋，动作放慢半拍
scene: 葬礼上没有人高声说话，连手机都收进了口袋。 The guests observed decorum even when the speech went wrong.
sceneCN: 这里 decorum 指合乎场合、保持端庄的举止（第 1 个义项：得体举止）；句意为即使致辞出了差错，宾客们仍遵守礼仪。

pos.zh: 礼仪；得体；端庄；合乎场合的举止

senses.title: Proper behaviour in public
senses.definition: conformity to accepted standards of polite behaviour in public
senses.definitionCN: 符合公共场合公认的礼貌行为标准
senses.example: The guests observed decorum even when the speech went wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 即使致辞出了差错，宾客们仍遵守礼仪。
senses.why: The Latin word named 'that which is fitting'; decorum is the behaviour that fits a room the way a key fits a lock.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词命名「合适之物」；decorum 就是像钥匙配锁那样契合场合的行为。

senses.title: A dignified appearance
senses.definition: an impression of seriousness, self-control and good form
senses.definitionCN: 严肃、自持与良好仪态给人的印象
senses.example: He received the award with quiet decorum.
senses.exampleCN: 他以安静的端庄接受了奖项。
senses.why: Appearance is the visible edge of behaviour: a straightened back and a low voice announce that the occasion is being respected.
senses.whyCN: 仪表是行为可见的边缘：挺直的背与压低的声音宣告对场合的尊重。

senses.title: Rules of a formal occasion
senses.definition: the set of customs expected at a ceremony or formal event
senses.definitionCN: 典礼或正式活动中被期待的一套习俗
senses.example: The ushers were briefed on the decorum of the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 引座员被告知典礼的礼仪要求。
senses.why: When many people share one event, expected behaviour becomes a script, and decorum is the script being followed.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人共享一个场合，被期待的行为就变成脚本，而 decorum 就是被遵循的脚本。

senses.title: Suitability of style
senses.definition: in literary criticism, the fitting of style to subject and occasion
senses.definitionCN: 在文学批评中，指风格与题材、场合的相称
senses.example: Classical critics made decorum a rule of style.
senses.exampleCN: 古典批评家把得体定为风格规则。
senses.why: A style is also behaviour: a grand subject refuses a joke, and the critic calls the refusal decorum.
senses.whyCN: 风格也是一种行为：宏大的题材拒绝玩笑，而批评家把这种拒绝称为得体。

senses.title: Composure under pressure
senses.definition: calm and correct behaviour maintained when something goes wrong
senses.definitionCN: 出差错时仍保持的镇定与正确举止
senses.example: She kept her decorum while the accusation was read aloud.
senses.exampleCN: 指控被朗读时，她仍保持镇定得体。
senses.why: The test of a standard is the moment it becomes inconvenient; decorum is most visible when it costs something.
senses.whyCN: 标准在它变得不方便的那一刻才受到检验；得体在需要付出代价时最为显眼。

senses.title: Ceremonial order
senses.definition: the prescribed order and manner of a formal ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 正式仪式规定的次序与方式
senses.example: The procession followed the decorum of the old rite.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍遵循古老仪式的既定次序。
senses.why: A ceremony is a sequence that must not be rearranged, and decorum is that sequence made visible in bodies.
senses.whyCN: 典礼是一套不可重排的次序，而得体就是这套次序在身体上的显现。

senses.title: Expected tone in scholarship
senses.titleCN: 学术写作中的得体语气
senses.definition: the tone and restraint expected in academic or professional writing
senses.definitionCN: 学术或专业写作中被期待的语调与克制
senses.example: The journal asked for decorum in the response.
senses.exampleCN: 期刊要求回应保持学术得体。
senses.why: Written exchange has its own room to fit: certain claims can be made, but not in certain voices.
senses.whyCN: 书面往来也有自己要契合的房间：某些主张可以提出，但不能以某些声音提出。

senses.title: Outward correctness as a mask
senses.definition: correct outward form that may conceal disorder underneath
senses.definitionCN: 外表的正确可能掩盖内在的失序
senses.example: The family maintained decorum while the argument continued upstairs.
senses.exampleCN: 楼上的争吵还在继续，一家人却维持着表面的得体。
senses.why: Form can be kept after feeling has gone, so the word can name a surface that no longer reports what is beneath it.
senses.whyCN: 感受消失后形式仍可维持，因此这个词也能命名一个不再反映内里的表面。

intro.en: Decorum is Latin for 'that which is fitting', from a root meaning grace and dignity.
intro.cn: decorum 是拉丁语「合适之物」的意思，词根意为优雅与尊严。

items.en: English borrowed decorum in the 17c. as a term of social and literary criticism.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 decorum，作为社会与文学批评的术语。

items.en: Decorum was the neuter of decorus 'fitting, graceful', used as a noun for what is proper.
items.cn: decorum 是 decorus「合适、优雅」的中性形式，作名词指合宜之物。

items.en: Decus meant 'grace, dignity, ornament', and gives decorate and decoration through related forms.
items.cn: decus 意为「优雅、尊严、装饰」，通过相关形式产生 decorate 与 decoration。

items.en: The impersonal verb decet 'it is fitting' states the standard that decorum later names.
items.cn: 无人称动词 decet「这是合适的」陈述了 decorum 后来命名的标准。

items.en: From public manners the word moved to literary style and then to any setting where a correct form is expected.
items.cn: 这个词从公共礼仪转向文学风格，再转向任何期待正确形式的场合。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the fitting root; the near-meaning group names codes of proper behaviour.
note.cn: 形近组共享「合适」词根；近义组列出得体行为的各种规范。

entries.definition: calm seriousness that earns respect.

abstract.en: Form can outlive feeling, which is why decorum can also be a mask.
abstract.cn: 形式可以比感受活得更久，所以得体也可能是一张面具。

abstract.en: Every occasion has a shape, and decorum is the body agreeing to that shape.

definition_zh: 民族学；人种学；对民族的比较研究
definition_en: the comparative study of peoples and their cultures
core_image: 把许多民族的语言、亲缘与器物摆在一张长桌上比较
scene: 博物馆的展柜按语言与亲缘把各民族的器物并排摆开，这种排列背后是一门比较的学问。 Comparative ethnology groups peoples by language, kinship, and material culture.
sceneCN: 这里 ethnology 是「民族学」（第 1 个义项：对各民族进行比较研究的学科）；句意：比较民族学按语言、亲缘关系与物质文化给各民族归类。

pos.zh: 民族学；人种学

senses.title: The comparative study of peoples
senses.definition: the branch of learning that compares the cultures, languages, and social forms of different peoples
senses.definitionCN: 比较不同民族的文化、语言与社会形态的学科
senses.example: Ethnology asks why neighbouring peoples organise kinship so differently.
senses.exampleCN: 民族学追问：为什么相邻民族的亲属制度差别如此之大。
senses.why: Greek logos means reasoned account, so ethnology is not the writing of one people but reasoned comparison across many, which is why the word names a general science.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 logos 意为有理据的论说，所以 ethnology 不是写下某一个民族，而是对许多民族作有理据的比较，因此它命名的是一门总体性的学问。

senses.title: The study of origins and distribution
senses.definition: the older programme of classifying peoples by origin, migration, and physical or cultural traits
senses.definitionCN: 较早的研究纲领，按起源、迁徙以及体质或文化特征给民族分类
senses.example: Nineteenth-century ethnology often mixed classification with speculation.
senses.exampleCN: 十九世纪的民族学常把分类与猜测混在一起。
senses.why: When the discipline was young, its main task was to place peoples on a map of descent and migration, and that historical programme still colours one sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科年轻时，主要任务是把各民族放到血统与迁徙的地图上，这个历史阶段的纲领至今仍构成该词的一个义项。

senses.title: Knowledge of one people or region
senses.titleCN: 对某一民族或地区的研究
senses.definition: the accumulated body of study devoted to a particular people or area
senses.definitionCN: 针对某个民族或某个地区积累起来的研究成果
senses.example: The museum holds a strong collection in the ethnology of the northern peoples.
senses.exampleCN: 这家博物馆在北方各民族的民族学研究上收藏颇丰。
senses.why: Like other names ending in -ology, it can shift from the whole discipline to the total knowledge about one object, so a library can hold the ethnology of a single region.
senses.whyCN: 和其他以 -ology 结尾的学科名一样，它可以从整门学科转指关于某一对象的全部知识，所以一座图书馆可以收藏某一地区的民族学研究。

intro.en: Ethnology joins Greek ethnos, a people, with -logia, from logos, reasoned account or study.
intro.cn: ethnology 由希腊语 ethnos（民族）与 -logia（源自 logos，论说、研究）组合而成。

items.en: Ethnos means a people or a nation, a group sharing descent and custom.
items.cn: ethnos 指民族或族群，即共享血统与习俗的群体。

items.en: Logos means word, account, or reasoned discourse.
items.cn: logos 指言词、叙述或有理据的论说。

items.en: The ending -logia names a field of study or a body of accounts.
items.cn: 词尾 -logia 表示某一研究领域或一批论述。

items.en: Scholars of the eighteenth century coin ethnologia for the study of peoples.
items.cn: 十八世纪的学者造出 ethnologia 一词，指对民族的研究。

items.en: English adopts ethnology for the classification and comparison of peoples.
items.cn: 英语采用 ethnology，指对各民族的分类与比较。

items.en: As anthropology takes over fieldwork, ethnology narrows toward comparison and regional knowledge.
items.cn: 随着人类学接管田野工作，ethnology 的范围收窄，转向比较与区域知识。

note.en: Ethnology is the comparing half of the ethno- family, next to its own adjective and person noun, and to the neighbouring social sciences.
note.cn: ethnology 是 ethno- 词族中「比较研究」的那一半，与它自己的形容词、人物名词以及相邻的社会科学为伍。

normal.en: Compare -graphy and -logy: writing one people, versus reasoning about many.
normal.cn: 对比 -graphy 与 -logy：一个是写下一个民族，一个是对许多民族作论说。

abstract.en: See a long table with the languages and kinship terms of many peoples laid out side by side.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，上面并排摊着许多民族的语言与亲属称谓，对应第 1 个义项的「比较研究」。

abstract.en: See lines drawn on a map of migrations, arrows meeting and splitting over the centuries.
abstract.cn: 想象一张迁徙地图上画出的线条，箭头在数百年间汇聚又分叉，对应第 2 个义项的「起源与分布」。

abstract.en: See one shelf in a library given wholly to a single northern people.
abstract.cn: 想象图书馆里整整一层书架只放关于某一个北方民族的研究，对应第 3 个义项的「区域知识」。

examples.en: Ethnology compares the kinship systems of neighbouring peoples.
examples.cn: 民族学比较相邻各民族的亲属制度。

examples.en: He teaches ethnology in a museum studies programme.
examples.cn: 他在一个博物馆研究项目中教授民族学。

examples.en: The library keeps a full run of the journal of ethnology.
examples.cn: 图书馆保存着这份民族学期刊的完整过刊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ethno 民族 + logy 学问」——研究各民族的学问；这只是拆词联想，与严格的词源考证并不等同。

root: 希腊语 ethnos（民族、族群）+ logos（论说、道理）→ -logia（某类研究）→ 新拉丁语 ethnologia → 英语 ethnology，核心义「对各民族作有理据的比较研究」。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers the whole comparative discipline, then the older programme of origins and distribution, then the accumulated knowledge of one people or region.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先指整门比较性的学科，再指较早的起源与分布研究纲领，最后指关于某一民族或地区积累起来的知识。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many peoples laid side by side on one long table for comparison.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多民族被并排摆在一张长桌上作比较。

branches.en: The comparative discipline is the central sense of the word.
branches.cn: 比较性的学科是这个词的核心义项。

branches.en: Classifying peoples by origin is the historical programme inside the discipline.
branches.cn: 按起源给民族分类，是这门学科内部的历史纲领。

branches.en: Knowledge of one region is the discipline applied to a single object.
branches.cn: 关于某一地区的知识，是这门学科落到单一对象上的用法。

branches.en: Comparison and classification used to be two names for one task.
branches.cn: 比较与分类一度是同一件事的两个名字。

branches.en: Origins are argued from regional knowledge, and regional knowledge is organised by origin.
branches.cn: 起源问题靠区域知识来论证，区域知识又按起源来组织。

intro.en: Ethnology is a Greek compound: ethnos, a people, plus -logy from logos, reasoned account.
intro.cn: ethnology 是希腊语复合词：ethnos（民族）加 -logy（源自 logos，有理据的论说）。

latinIntro.en: New Latin ethnologia fixed the shape of the word before English borrowed it.
latinIntro.cn: 新拉丁语 ethnologia 在英语借入之前就固定了这个词的词形。

items.example: Ethnos is the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: ethnos 是这个复合词的前半部分。

items.example: Logos gives the reasoning half of the word.
items.exampleCN: logos 提供这个词「论说」的那一半。

items.meaning: a field of study or discourse
items.meaningCN: 表示某类研究或论述的后缀
items.example: The suffix -logia names whole disciplines.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -logia 用来命名整门学科。

items.example: The suffix -logy also builds biology.
The prefix ethno- also builds ethnography.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ethno- 也构成 ethnography。

items.example: Ethnologia is the learned Latin form.
items.exampleCN: ethnologia 是学术拉丁语形式。

items.example: Ethnology keeps the comparing sense.

items.meaningCN: 由名词构成形容词的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ical forms ethnological.
Ethnological collections are grouped by region.
items.exampleCN: 民族学藏品按地区分组。

items.meaningCN: 表示「从事某事的人」的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ist forms ethnologist.

definition_zh: v. 通勤；减刑 n. 通勤路程
definition_en: to travel regularly to and from work
core_image: 清晨地铁站里一排排赶着上班的人
scene: 她每天坐地铁通勤到市中心上班。 She commutes to the city centre by subway every day.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：commute 指通勤；句意是她每天坐地铁通勤到市中心上班。

pos.zh: 通勤；减刑
通勤路程

senses.title: To travel to work regularly
senses.definition: to make the same journey to work and back each day
senses.definitionCN: 每天往返同一段上班路程
senses.example: He commutes an hour each way.
senses.exampleCN: 他单程通勤一小时。
senses.why: Latin commutare means to exchange.

senses.title: To reduce a punishment

senses.definitionCN: 把重刑改为较轻的处罚
senses.example: The governor commuted the sentence.

senses.why: The legal sense keeps the old idea of exchange.
senses.whyCN: 法律义保留了「交换」的旧意。

intro.en: Commute first meant to exchange, then to travel back and forth.
intro.cn: commute 最初意为交换，后指往返。

items.en: Mutare means to change.

items.en: Commutare means to exchange.

items.en: Railways made commuting a daily trip.

items.en: Commuting now shapes city life.
items.cn: 现代通勤塑造了城市生活。

entries.definition: To go from place to place.

normalIntro.cn: commute 就是把「家」与「工作」来回交换。

normal.en: Commutare means to exchange.

examples.en: Many workers commute into the capital.
