definition_zh: 白蚁；（喻）从内部慢慢蛀空组织的人或事物
definition_en: a pale, soft-bodied social insect that feeds on wood and lives in colonies with distinct castes
core_image: 一块外表完好的木板被撬开，里面是无数细小管道，像被谁用针一层层掏空，只剩一层薄壳
scene: 老房子的地板踩上去还是硬的，可撬开一角，底下已经全是细土一样的碎渣。 One termite is harmless, but a colony can hollow a beam without touching its surface.
sceneCN: 这里 termite 指「白蚁」（第 1 个义项：体色浅、体软、蛀食木材的群居昆虫）；句意为一只白蚁无害，但一个蚁群能在不碰表面的情况下把梁掏空。

pos.zh: 白蚁；白蚁类

senses.title: The pale wood-eating social insect
senses.titleCN: 浅色、蛀食木材的群居昆虫
senses.definition: a soft-bodied, usually pale insect of the cockroach lineage that lives in colonies and feeds mainly on wood
senses.definitionCN: 体软、通常色浅、属蟑螂谱系、群居并以木材为主食的昆虫
senses.example: One termite is harmless, but a colony can hollow a beam.
senses.exampleCN: 一只白蚁无害，但一个蚁群能把梁掏空。
senses.why: the word names the animal, and the whole vocabulary of damage, mounds and castes is built outward from it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名动物，关于损坏、蚁丘与品级的整套词汇都由它向外生长出来。

senses.title: The colony with its castes
senses.definition: the organised society of workers, soldiers and reproductives living in one nest
senses.definitionCN: 在同一巢中生活的工蚁、兵蚁与繁殖个体组成的有组织社会
senses.example: The termite colony was three metres deep and twenty years old.
senses.exampleCN: 这个白蚁群深达三米，已有二十年。
senses.why: because individuals are almost never seen alone, the singular often stands for the whole society.
senses.whyCN: 因为个体几乎从不单独出现，单数常代指整个社会。

senses.title: A named ecological type
senses.definition: a kind identified by habit, such as subterranean, drywood or mound-building termites
senses.definitionCN: 按习性区分的类型，如地下白蚁、干木白蚁、筑丘白蚁
senses.example: Drywood termites need no contact with soil at all.
senses.exampleCN: 干木白蚁完全不需要接触土壤。
senses.why: types are distinguished by where they live, so a qualifier carries the whole difference.
senses.whyCN: 类型由栖息处区分，因此一个限定语承担了全部差别。

senses.title: A destroyer of timber in buildings
senses.definition: the species regarded as a structural pest because it consumes wood from the inside
senses.definitionCN: 因从内部吃空木材而被视为结构害虫的物种
senses.example: Termite damage went unnoticed until the floor sagged.
senses.exampleCN: 白蚁的损坏直到地板下沉才被发现。
senses.why: the damage is described by its agent because the insect leaves a hollow shell rather than a visible hole.
senses.whyCN: 损坏由施害者来描述，因为昆虫留下的是空壳而不是明显的洞。

senses.title: A decomposer of dead wood
senses.definition: the ecological role of breaking down fallen timber and returning nutrients to the soil
senses.definitionCN: 分解倒木、把养分归还土壤的生态角色
senses.example: Termites clear dead wood faster than fungi in dry forests.
senses.exampleCN: 在干燥森林里，白蚁分解枯木比真菌更快。
senses.why: the same activity that ruins a house recycles a forest, so the word carries both judgements.
senses.whyCN: 毁屋与还林是同一种活动，因此这个词同时承载两种判断。

senses.title: A subject for symbiosis research
senses.definition: the insect as a host whose gut microbes digest wood, studied as a model of symbiosis
senses.definitionCN: 肠道微生物帮它消化木材，因而作为共生模型被研究的昆虫
senses.example: The termite depends on microbes it passes to its young.
senses.exampleCN: 白蚁依赖它传给后代的微生物。
senses.why: a striking biological dependency makes the animal a research system, and the name stands for the system.
senses.whyCN: 一种显著的生物依赖使这种动物成为研究体系，其名称代表这个体系。

senses.title: A builder of ventilated mounds
senses.titleCN: 建造通风蚁丘的建筑者
senses.definition: the mound-building species whose structures regulate heat and gas exchange
senses.definitionCN: 所筑结构能调节热量与气体交换的筑丘物种
senses.example: The termite mound keeps a steady temperature through the day.
senses.exampleCN: 白蚁丘昼夜保持稳定温度。
senses.why: architecture is attributed to a builder, so the insect's name travels to the structure it makes.
senses.whyCN: 建筑被归给建造者，因此昆虫之名也移向它所造的结构。

senses.title: Figurative: something hollowing from within
senses.definition: figurative, a person or institution that undermines a group secretly and gradually
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指暗中、逐步蛀空某个群体的人或机构
senses.example: The report called the smuggling network a termite in the customs service.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把走私网络称作海关内部的白蚁。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps only the hidden, internal, gradual hollowing, which is exactly what the insect does.
senses.whyCN: 比喻只保留隐蔽、内部、渐进的掏空，而这正是这种昆虫所做的事。

intro.en: Termite is a late eighteenth-century learned word from Latin termes, the name for a woodworm; its earlier English name was the misleading white ant.
intro.cn: termite 是 18 世纪后期的学术词，出自拉丁 termes「木蠹虫」；其较早英语名是易致误解的 white ant。

items.en: Latin termes named a woodworm or a gnawing insect, and English naturalists revived it for the tropical wood-eating insect.
items.cn: 拉丁 termes 指木蠹虫或蛀咬的昆虫，英语博物学家把它复活用于热带蛀木昆虫。

items.en: Source uncertain (root): the origin of Latin termes itself is unresolved; a link to a verb for gnawing has been suggested, but the form given for it is reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根）：拉丁 termes 本身的来源无定论；与某个表示「啃咬」的动词的联系属提议，且所给形式为重构。

items.en: The older English name white ant treated the insect as a pale ant, a mistake that modern classification has corrected.
items.cn: 较早的英语名 white ant 把它当作浅色的蚂蚁，这一错误已被现代分类纠正。

items.en: Termites are now placed with cockroaches rather than with ants, a result of twentieth-century anatomical and molecular work.
items.cn: 白蚁现被归入蟑螂一类而非蚂蚁，这是 20 世纪解剖与分子研究的结果。

items.en: As timber construction spread, the word became a household word for structural damage and for the inspection trade.
items.cn: 随着木结构建筑普及，这个词成为关于结构损坏与检查行业的日常词。

items.en: The image of hidden internal hollowing produced the political metaphor of a termite inside an institution.
items.cn: 隐蔽内部掏空的意象产生了「机构内部白蚁」的政治比喻。

note.en: Group one separates termite from the insects it is historically confused with; group two separates the animal from its products and its metaphors.
note.cn: 第一组区分 termite 与其历史上易混的昆虫；第二组区分动物本身与其产物、比喻。

entries.definition: The insect once called a white ant; ants are darker, have a narrow waist and belong to a different order.
entries.definitionCN: 曾被叫作白蚁的昆虫；蚂蚁颜色更深、腰细，且属另一目。

entries.definition: An old English name for the termite, still met in older books; the insect is neither white nor an ant.
entries.definitionCN: 白蚁的旧英语名，仍见于旧书；它既不白也不是蚂蚁。

entries.definition: The nest or mound itself, not the insect; the -arium suffix marks a place.
entries.definitionCN: 巢或丘本身，而非昆虫；-arium 后缀标记场所。

entries.definition: A product that kills termites, built with the -cide suffix of killing.
entries.definitionCN: 杀白蚁的产品，由表「杀」的 -cide 后缀构成。

entries.definition: Woodworm names the larvae of wood-boring beetles; Latin termes covered similar gnawers before it was fixed to termites.
entries.definitionCN: woodworm 指蛀木甲虫的幼虫；拉丁 termes 在被固定指白蚁前也涵盖类似的蛀虫。

entries.definition: A carpenter ant excavates galleries in wood but does not eat it; a termite actually digests the wood.
entries.definitionCN: 木匠蚁在木中挖道但不吃木；白蚁则真正消化木材。

entries.definition: Borer names any animal that drills into wood or stems; termite names a particular social insect.
entries.definitionCN: borer 指任何钻入木材或茎的动物；termite 指特定的社会性昆虫。

entries.definition: Decomposer is a functional role in a food web; termite is the organism that fills it in dry forests.
entries.definitionCN: decomposer 是食物网中的功能角色；白蚁是在干燥森林中承担该角色的生物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin source, the real misnomer and real trade terms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实拉丁来源、真实误称与真实行业用语。

normal.en: Latin termes meant a woodworm, and English took it for the tropical wood-eater.
normal.cn: 拉丁 termes 指木蠹虫，英语用它指热带的蛀木者。

normal.en: The old name white ant is a double mistake: not white, not an ant.
normal.cn: 旧名 white ant 是双重错误：既不白，也不是蚂蚁。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: termite damage, termite mound, termite inspection.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：白蚁损坏、白蚁丘、白蚁检查。

normal.en: Termites are now classified with cockroaches, not with ants.
normal.cn: 白蚁现被归入蟑螂一类，而非蚂蚁。

normal.en: Termites digest wood with microbes in their gut, a standard case of symbiosis.
normal.cn: 白蚁靠肠道微生物消化木材，是共生的标准案例。

abstract.en: Picture a beam that sounds solid when tapped and is dust inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一根梁，敲起来是实的，里面却是粉。

abstract.en: Picture a city of narrow corridors built without a single window.
abstract.cn: 想象一座全是窄走廊、没有一扇窗的城市。

abstract.en: Picture a flaw that eats an organisation while its reports look clean.
abstract.cn: 想象一个缺陷在吞噬机构，而报告看起来一切正常。

examples.en: Termites reached the sill through a mud tube built in the dark.
examples.cn: 白蚁沿着在暗处筑成的泥管到达了门槛。

examples.en: The mound was opened and the termites were gone within an hour.
examples.cn: 蚁丘被打开后，白蚁一小时内就撤空了。

examples.en: Inspectors look for termites before any sale of the house.
examples.cn: 房屋出售前，检查人员会找白蚁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ter（土）+ mite」——在土里做巢、把木头蛀成粉的虫 → 白蚁

root: 拉丁 termes「木蠹虫、蛀虫」，英语在 18 世纪后期借入指白蚁；拉丁词本身的更深来源不确定，与「啃咬」动词的联系仅为重构性提议。旧英语名 white ant 属误称。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one hidden hollowing: a pale insect eats wood from inside, and the word then names the colony, a type, a structural pest, a decomposer, a symbiosis model, a mound builder, and finally a person who undermines from within.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一种隐蔽的掏空展开：浅色昆虫从内部吃木；词语随后指群体、类型、结构害虫、分解者、共生模型、筑丘者，最后指从内部蛀空的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beam that looks intact until the shell is lifted and only dust remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根看似完好的梁，撬开薄壳后只剩粉末。

branches.en: INSECT AND SOCIETY: one animal, then the caste system it never leaves.
branches.cn: 昆虫与社会：一只动物，然后是它从不脱离的品级体系。

branches.en: HABIT TYPES: subterranean, drywood and mound builders are one word plus a qualifier.
branches.cn: 习性命型：地下、干木、筑丘都是一个词加限定语。

branches.en: TWO VERDICTS: destroyer of a building, restorer of a forest.
branches.cn: 两种裁断：建筑的破坏者，森林的恢复者。

items.example: The Latin word named a wood-eater long before the tropics were studied.

definition_zh: 推断；演绎；由……推出；推导
definition_en: to reach a conclusion by reasoning from evidence or from general principles
core_image: 一串脚印从泥地延伸到矮墙下，看的人顺着痕迹一步步把结论领出来
scene: 侦探看到窗台上的灰被擦去一半，便由这条痕迹推出有人从窗子进出。 From the half-wiped dust the detective deduced that someone had used the window.
sceneCN: 这里指依据现场痕迹推出事实（第 6 个义项：由实物线索推断出事实）；句意：侦探从被擦去一半的灰尘推断有人用过那扇窗。

pos.zh: 推断；演绎；推导

senses.title: To reach a conclusion by reasoning
senses.definition: to work out a conclusion from evidence rather than from direct observation
senses.definitionCN: 由证据而非直接观察得出一个结论
senses.example: From the marks on the wall they deduced that the water had once been higher.
senses.exampleCN: 他们从墙上的痕迹推断出水位曾经更高。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to lead down, so the mind is led from the evidence down to the conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为向下引领，心智被从证据一路领到结论。

senses.title: To derive a case from premises (logic)
senses.titleCN: 在逻辑上由前提出发推出
senses.definition: in logic, to derive a particular statement from general premises by a valid step
senses.definitionCN: 在逻辑中，由一般前提出发经有效步骤推出具体陈述
senses.example: From the two premises the class deduced that no exception could exist.
senses.exampleCN: 由这两个前提，全班推出不可能存在例外。
senses.why: Logic made the downward leading a formal procedure with rules that fix what may follow.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学把这种向下引领变成有规则约束的正式程序，规定什么可以推出。

senses.title: To trace something to its source (formal)
senses.definition: in formal or older usage, to trace a fact or a word back to its origin
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或较早用法中，把某个事实或词语追溯到其来源
senses.example: The custom may be deduced from an older harvest rite.
senses.exampleCN: 这一习俗也许可以追溯到一种更古老的收获仪式。
senses.why: Led down also means followed back along a chain, which is how origins are recovered.
senses.whyCN: 向下引领也意味着沿链条反推，追溯来源正是这样完成的。

senses.title: To work out a meaning from context
senses.definition: to infer the sense of a word or a passage from the surrounding text
senses.definitionCN: 由上下文推断词或段落的意思
senses.example: Readers deduce the meaning of an unfamiliar word from the sentence around it.
senses.exampleCN: 读者从周围的句子推断出生词的意思。
senses.why: Language gives partial evidence, and the mind fills the rest by the same leading-down path.
senses.whyCN: 语言提供部分证据，心智沿同一条向下引领的路径把其余部分补上。

senses.title: To derive a rule from data
senses.definition: to extract a general rule or pattern from a set of observations
senses.definitionCN: 从一组观察中抽出一条一般规律或模式
senses.example: The analysts deduced a seasonal pattern from three years of sales.
senses.exampleCN: 分析师从三年的销售数据推出一个季节性规律。
senses.why: Data is the premise and the rule is the conclusion, so the verb names the path between them.
senses.whyCN: 数据是前提，规律是结论，这个动词命名的是两者之间的路径。

senses.title: To infer facts from physical clues
senses.definition: to reconstruct what happened from traces left in the physical world
senses.definitionCN: 根据物质世界留下的痕迹重建事情经过
senses.example: From the half-wiped dust the detective deduced that someone had used the window.
senses.exampleCN: 侦探从被擦去一半的灰尘推断有人用过那扇窗。
senses.why: Clues are premises written in matter, and the detective's work is the old verb in its most dramatic form.
senses.whyCN: 线索是用物质写成的前提，侦探的工作就是这个古老动词最戏剧化的形态。

senses.title: To derive a formula or result (mathematics)
senses.definition: in mathematics, to obtain a result by a sequence of valid steps
senses.definitionCN: 在数学中，通过一系列有效步骤得到结果
senses.example: The students deduced the area formula from the rectangle.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们由矩形面积推出了那个面积公式。
senses.why: Mathematics is the home of the downward step, where each line must follow from the one before.
senses.whyCN: 数学是这种向下推步的主场，每一行都必须由前一行推出。

senses.title: To work out consequences of a theory
senses.definition: to set out what must follow if a theory or an assumption is accepted
senses.definitionCN: 说明若接受某个理论或假设，必然会出现什么
senses.example: If the model is right, we can deduce where the particles should appear.
senses.exampleCN: 如果模型正确，我们就能推知粒子应当出现在哪里。
senses.why: A theory is judged by its consequences, and drawing them out is the everyday work of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 理论靠其后果受检验，把后果推出来正是这个动词的日常工作。

intro.en: Deduce comes from a Latin verb meaning to lead down or to draw off, built from a prefix of downward movement and the verb for leading. English took it in the sixteenth century, and logic fixed the sense of deriving a conclusion.
intro.cn: 本词出自一个表示向下引领或引出的拉丁动词，由表示向下的前缀与表示引领的动词构成。英语在十六世纪借入，逻辑学固定了「推出结论」的含义。

items.en: Ducere meant to lead or to draw, and it stands behind many English words of conducting and producing.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为引领、牵引，英语中许多表示引导与产出的词都出自它。

items.en: The prefix meant down or away, so the compound pictured a movement downward along a path.
items.cn: 这个前缀表示向下或离开，因此复合词描绘的是沿路径向下的移动。

items.en: The Latin verb meant to lead down or to draw off, and also to derive one thing from another.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为向下引领或引出，也指由一事物导出另一事物。

items.en: Medieval logic fixed the word for the step from general premises to a particular conclusion.
items.cn: 中世纪逻辑学把这个词固定为从一般前提走向具体结论的那一步。

items.en: English borrowed it in the sixteenth century, when logic and rhetoric were school subjects.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入，当时逻辑与修辞是学校科目。

items.en: Detection, mathematics and language teaching each gave the old step a new kind of premise.
items.cn: 侦查、数学与语言教学各自给这古老的一步配上新种类的前提。

note.en: The first group shares the leading root or its English forms; the second group names nearby kinds of reasoning and seeing. Deduce moves along a chain from premises to a conclusion, while discern grasps something faint or hidden by looking closely, so a chain of steps and an act of perception must be kept apart.
note.cn: 第一组共享引领词根或其英语形式；第二组是相邻的推理与察看。本词沿前提链一步步走向结论，辨察类词则靠细看抓住模糊或隐蔽之物，推理链与感知动作必须分开。

entries.definition: The conclusion drawn, and also the sum taken away from a total.
entries.definitionCN: 推出的结论，也指从总额中扣除的数额。

entries.definition: Of reasoning that starts from general rules, the opposite of inductive.
entries.definitionCN: 指从一般规则出发的推理，与归纳相对。

entries.definition: Able to be worked out from what is given.
entries.definitionCN: 可由已知条件推出的。

entries.definition: To subtract an amount; the money sense split off from the reasoning sense.
entries.definitionCN: 减去一笔数额；金额义从推理义分出来。

entries.definition: To reach a conclusion from evidence; it does not require a formal chain of steps.
entries.definitionCN: 由证据得出结论；不要求正式的步骤链。

entries.definition: To arrive at a final judgement; it names the end, not the path.
entries.definitionCN: 得出最终判断；指终点，而非路径。

entries.definition: To obtain something from a source, often a formula or a word.
entries.definitionCN: 从某个来源得到某物，常指公式或词语。

entries.definition: To think logically in general; it may move in either direction.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指合乎逻辑地思考；可向任一方向进行。

entries.definition: To find an answer by thinking; the plain everyday phrase behind the formal verb.
entries.definitionCN: 靠思考找出答案；是正式动词背后平实的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the leading root, the real family and the prepositions that mark the premise.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用引领词根、真实同族词，以及标记前提的介词。

normal.en: The root means to lead, so the verb is to be led from evidence down to a conclusion.
normal.cn: 词根意为引领，动词就是由证据被领到结论。

normal.en: The family runs deduction, deductive, deducible and the money verb deduct.
normal.cn: 同族词有推论、演绎的、可推断的，以及表示扣除的同根动词。

normal.en: The preposition is from: one deduces something from something else.
normal.cn: 介词用「由」：由某物推出另一物。

normal.en: Logic makes the step formal, and mathematics makes it visible line by line.
normal.cn: 逻辑使这步正式化，数学使它在每一行上可见。

normal.en: The detective sense is the most vivid: clues as premises written in matter.
normal.cn: 侦探义最生动：线索是用物质写成的前提。

abstract.en: Picture a path of stepping stones that only appears one stone at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一条踏脚石小路，每次只浮现一块石头。

abstract.en: Picture a locked box whose key is the shape of the lid, not a separate object.
abstract.cn: 想象一只锁箱，钥匙的形状就藏在盖子上，而不是另一件东西。

abstract.en: Picture a rope ladder let down rung by rung, each rung held by the one above.
abstract.cn: 想象一架绳梯逐级放下，每一级都由上面一级吊住。

examples.en: From the silence in the room she deduced that the news was bad.
examples.cn: 从屋里的沉默，她推断消息不好。

examples.en: We can deduce the age of the rock from the fossils in it.
examples.cn: 我们可以从岩石中的化石推断其年代。

examples.en: The rule can be deduced from a handful of examples.
examples.cn: 这条规律可以从少数几个例子推出。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「得」加「丢斯」——顺着脚印一级级往下领，最后领出结论：推断

root: 拉丁语「向下」前缀加「引领」动词构成「向下引出、导出」，中世纪逻辑学固定为「演绎推出」，十六世纪进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all lead from something given to something concluded: evidence, premises, an origin, a context, data, clues, axioms and a theory's consequences.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都是从已给之物走向结论：证据、前提、来源、语境、数据、线索、公理与理论的后果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of footprints running to a low wall while a watcher follows them step by step to the conclusion.
core.cn: 核心意象：一串脚印从泥地延伸到矮墙下，看的人顺着痕迹一步步把结论领出来。

branches.en: THE CLUES: reasoning from evidence, and reconstructing an event from physical traces.
branches.cn: 线索：由证据推理，以及由实物痕迹重建事件。

branches.en: THE FORMAL CHAIN: a conclusion drawn from premises, and the consequences of a theory.
branches.cn: 形式链：由前提推出结论，以及理论的必然后果。

branches.en: THE ORIGIN: a custom or a word traced back along a chain.
branches.cn: 来源：沿着链条反推的习俗或词语。

branches.en: THE CONTEXT: a meaning recovered from the surrounding words.
branches.cn: 语境：由周围词语复原出的含义。

branches.en: THE RULE AND THE FORMULA: a pattern drawn from data and a result derived in mathematics.
branches.cn: 规律与公式：由数据抽出的模式，以及数学中导出的结果。

intro.en: Deduce is a Latin verb of leading down, and its family supplies the noun of the conclusion, the adjective of the method and a separate verb for subtraction.
intro.cn: 本词是一个表示向下引领的拉丁动词，其词族提供表示结论的名词、描述方法的形容词，以及一个表示扣除的独立动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere and the prefix de- form the verb; the English endings were added later.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示引领的动词与表示向下的前缀构成这个动词，英语词尾是后加的。

items.example: It gives the movement its downward direction.
items.exampleCN: 它给这个移动以向下的方向。

items.example: The root supplies the pulling of the mind along.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供心智被一路牵引之意。

items.example: The verb is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: English shortened the Latin verb to its modern shape.
items.exampleCN: 英语把拉丁动词缩短为现代形式。

items.example: It builds the noun for the conclusion and for subtraction.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示结论与扣除的名词。

items.example: It builds the adjective for the method of reasoning.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述推理方法的形容词。

items.example: It builds the adjective for what can be worked out.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述可被推出的形容词。

items.example: It builds the noun for the statements one starts from.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示出发时所依据的陈述的名词。

items.example: It builds the verb for drawing a final judgement together.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示把判断收拢起来的动词。

definition_zh: n. 蜻蜓；空中猎手；蜻蜓纹样
definition_en: a long-bodied flying insect with two pairs of clear wings that hovers and hunts other insects in the air

pos.zh: 蜻蜓；空中猎手；蜻蜓纹样

senses.title: The insect
senses.definition: a flying insect with a long thin body and two pairs of clear wings that can hover and fly backwards
senses.definitionCN: （名词）身体细长、有两对透明翅膀、能悬停也能倒飞的昆虫
senses.example: A dragonfly hovered over the reeds and then darted away.

intro.en: Dragonfly is dragon plus fly, a fly as fierce as a dragon; the name appeared in the 17th century, replacing older English words such as adderbolt and horse-stinger, and it reflects the insect as a ruthless hunter rather than any fire.
intro.cn: dragonfly 由 dragon 加 fly 组成，像龙一样凶的蝇；这个名字出现在 17 世纪，取代了 adderbolt 一类旧英语词，它反映的是这种昆虫作为无情猎手的一面，与火无关。

items.en: Latin draco means a dragon or large serpent.
items.cn: 拉丁语 draco 意为龙或大蛇。

items.en: Old English fleoge means a fly.
items.cn: 古英语 fleoge 意为蝇。

items.en: English called the insect adderbolt or horse-stinger.
items.cn: 英语曾把这种昆虫叫作 adderbolt 或 horse-stinger。

items.en: The compound dragonfly is recorded in English.
items.cn: 复合词 dragonfly 在英语中被记录下来。

items.en: Writers describe the dragonfly as a hunter of mosquitoes.
items.cn: 作者把蜻蜓描述为捕食蚊子的猎手。

items.en: The dragonfly becomes a favourite motif in jewellery.
items.cn: 蜻蜓成为首饰中常见的纹样。

note.en: Dragonfly is a fly as fierce as a dragon; its look-alikes share dragon or fly, and its neighbours name other insects seen over water.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long-bodied insect hovering above reeds with four net-veined wings while six legs form a basket in the air

intro.cn: dragonfly 由 dragon 加 fly 组成；同一个 fly 造出 damselfly 与 mayfly，而希腊语词根 odon- 与拉丁语词根 libell- 从另一个方向指称有齿的猎手与小书。

definition_zh: 绕过；规避；回避；设法避开
definition_en: to go around a place, rule or difficulty instead of facing it directly
core_image: 一道封锁线横在路口，车队拐进旁边的小路，从侧面绕过了检查点
scene: 出口禁令下来后，这家公司把货先运到第三个国家再转运。 The firm routed its shipments through a third country to circumvent the export ban.
sceneCN: 这里指绕开一条法规的限制（第 2 个义项：规避法律或规则）；句意为这家公司借第三国转运来规避出口禁令。图中可辨识物件：封锁线、岔出的小路、绕行的货车。

pos.zh: 绕过；规避；回避

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「规避；绕行」
由该动词加已然词尾构成，义为「被绕过的；被规避的」
由该动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「规避性的」
由该动词加表示倾向的形容词尾构成，义为「倾向于规避的」（少用）
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「规避者」（少用）

senses.title: To go around a place
senses.definition: to travel around a town, barrier or defended area rather than through it
senses.definitionCN: 不走某座城镇、障碍或防区的正面，而是从外围过去
senses.example: The convoy circumvented the flooded valley by the eastern road.
senses.exampleCN: 车队走东边的路绕过了被淹的河谷。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to come around, and the physical circle around a place is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词本义是「绕到周围」，绕着地方走一圈是最古老的义项。

senses.title: To evade a rule
senses.definition: to avoid the effect of a law or regulation by using a route it did not cover
senses.definitionCN: 利用法规没有覆盖的路径，避开它的效力
senses.example: Some importers circumvent the quota by splitting the shipment.
senses.exampleCN: 一些进口商把货拆单，以规避配额。
senses.why: A rule draws a line; going around it is the same geometry applied to law.
senses.whyCN: 规则画了一条线，绕过去就是把同一几何关系用到法律上。

senses.title: To sidestep a difficulty
senses.definition: to avoid dealing with a hard question or obstacle directly
senses.definitionCN: 不正面处理难题或障碍
senses.example: The report circumvented the central question of cost.
senses.exampleCN: 报告绕开了成本这个核心问题。
senses.why: A difficulty stands in the road, and the verb chooses the path that leaves it untouched.
senses.whyCN: 困难立在路中，这个动词选了那条不去碰它的路。

senses.title: To get around a control
senses.definition: to defeat a check, filter or supervisory mechanism without formally breaking it
senses.definitionCN: 在不正式违反的前提下让核查、过滤或监管失效
senses.example: The app circumvented the parental lock with a hidden menu.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用用隐藏菜单绕过了家长锁。
senses.why: Control systems are walls with gates, and the word describes finding the part with no gate.
senses.whyCN: 管控系统是有门的墙，这个词描述的是找到没有门的那一段。

senses.title: To avoid an opponent
senses.definition: to avoid meeting an opposing force by moving around its position
senses.definitionCN: 通过绕过对方的阵地而不与其正面交战
senses.example: The unit circumvented the patrol and reached the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 这支部队绕过巡逻队抵达桥头。
senses.why: Military usage keeps the spatial core: avoid the strong point, reach the objective.
senses.whyCN: 军事用法保留空间内核：避开强点，抵达目标。

senses.title: To avoid a fee or tax
senses.definition: to arrange affairs so that a charge legally applies to someone else or not at all
senses.definitionCN: 通过安排使某项收费依法落到别人头上或干脆不产生
senses.example: The trust was set up to circumvent the inheritance tax.
senses.exampleCN: 这个信托就是为规避遗产税设立的。
senses.why: Money follows routes, and the word supplies the route that misses the toll booth.
senses.whyCN: 钱走路线，这个词提供了那条错过收费亭的路线。

senses.title: To work around a problem
senses.definition: to reach a goal by an indirect method when the direct one is blocked
senses.definitionCN: 在直接方法行不通时，用间接办法达到目的
senses.example: The engineers circumvented the faulty sensor with a manual override.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师用手动接管绕过了失灵的传感器。
senses.why: This is the constructive side of the word: the obstacle stays, but it is no longer on the path.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词的建设性一面：障碍还在，只是不再挡在路上。

senses.title: To bypass a system limit
senses.definition: to get past a technical restriction, lock or limit without disabling it
senses.definitionCN: 在不关掉技术限制的情况下越过它
senses.example: A crafted request circumvents the rate limit on the server.
senses.exampleCN: 一个构造的请求绕过了服务器上的速率限制。
senses.why: Digital systems reproduce walls and gates, so the old verb fits them exactly.
senses.whyCN: 数字系统复制了墙与门，这个古老的动词正好合身。

intro.en: Circumvent comes from Latin circumvenire, to come around or surround, from circum, around, and venire, to come. English extended the physical circle to rules and controls.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 circumvenire「绕到周围、包围」，由 circum「周围」与 venire「来」构成；英语把这一圈从空间扩展到规则与管控。

items.en: Circum meant around on all sides, and it is the same element in circle, circuit and circumference.
items.cn: 这个词意为「四周环绕」，也是 circle、circuit、circumference 中的同一成分。

items.en: Venire meant to come or go, and it supplies the second half of words such as intervene and prevent.
items.cn: 这个词意为「来、去」，提供 intervene、prevent 等词的后半部分。

items.en: The compound meant to come around, to surround, and in military writing to encircle an enemy.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为「绕到周围、包围」，在军事文献中指包抄敌军。

items.en: Latin also used the verb for getting around a person by trickery, which prepared the English sense of evasion.
items.cn: 拉丁语也用这个动词指以手段绕开某人，这为英语的「规避」义做了准备。

items.en: English adopted the verb in the fifteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain and is usually given only as that century.
items.cn: 英语十五世纪采用这个动词，确切首见年代不确定，通常只给「十五世纪」。

items.en: Law and computing both needed a word for going around a barrier, and the old verb filled both roles.
items.cn: 法律与计算机都需要一个表示「绕过屏障」的词，这个古老动词同时补上了两个位置。

note.en: The first group shares the circum prefix or looks close; the second group names neighbouring ideas of avoidance and bypass.
note.cn: 第一组与「circumvent」共享 circum 前缀或只是形近；第二组是与「回避、绕过」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of going around a rule or barrier.
entries.definitionCN: 指绕过规则或屏障这一行为的名词。

entries.definition: The distance around a circle; the prefix matches but the root is to carry.
entries.definitionCN: 指圆周长度；前缀相同，但词根是「携带」。

entries.definition: A condition around an event; the prefix matches but the root is to stand.
entries.definitionCN: 指事件周围的条件；前缀相同，词根是「站立」。

entries.definition: Cautious, literally looking around; the prefix matches but the root is to look.
entries.definitionCN: 指谨慎，字面是「环顾」；前缀相同，词根是「看」。

entries.definition: A closed path or a loop, related in meaning but formed on a different stem.
entries.definitionCN: 指闭合路径或回路，意义相关但词干不同。

entries.definition: To go around a town or a rule, the plainest equivalent.
entries.definitionCN: 指绕开城镇或规则，是最直白的对应说法。

entries.definition: To escape something by cleverness, with a stronger note of avoidance of duty.
entries.definitionCN: 指以巧计逃脱，更强调逃避责任。

entries.definition: To keep away from something, with no route image.
entries.definitionCN: 指远离某物，不含路线画面。

entries.definition: To step to one side, literally or figuratively.
entries.definitionCN: 指侧身避开，字面或比喻皆可。

entries.definition: To pass along the edge of something rather than through it.
entries.definitionCN: 指沿着边缘经过而不穿越。

entries.definition: To move quickly out of the way, often of a blow or a question.
entries.definitionCN: 指迅速闪开，多用于打击或问题。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the circle prefix, the come root, and the legal and technical phrases that keep the word current.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「圈」前缀、「来」词根，以及让这个词保持活跃的法律与技术搭配。

normal.en: Circum is around, so the word begins with a circle drawn around a barrier.
normal.cn: circum 是「周围」，所以这个词从围绕障碍画的一个圈开始。

normal.en: Venire is to come, the same root as intervene and prevent.
normal.cn: venire 是「来」，与 intervene、prevent 同根。

normal.en: Law says circumvent a rule; computing says circumvent a limit.
normal.cn: 法律说规避规则，计算机说绕过限制。

normal.en: Circumvent is not the same as break: the rule still stands, you simply avoid its reach.
normal.cn: 这个词不等于违反：规则仍在，只是避开它的触及范围。

normal.en: The old military sense was to encircle, which is why the word still feels like a manoeuvre.
normal.cn: 古代军事义是包抄，所以这个词至今带有调动的感觉。

abstract.en: To circumvent is to accept the wall and refuse the gate.
abstract.cn: 绕过，就是承认墙的存在，却拒绝走那扇门。

abstract.en: Every rule draws a line; every line has a place where it stops being watched.
abstract.cn: 每条规则都画一条线，而每条线都有不再被盯着的一段。

abstract.en: The shortest path is not always direct, and the word lives in that gap.
abstract.cn: 最短的路未必是直路，这个词就活在这个缝隙里。

examples.en: The supplier circumvented the ban by relabelling the goods.
examples.cn: 供应商改换货物标签以规避禁令。

examples.en: Drivers circumvent the closed bridge by a narrow riverside road.
examples.cn: 司机沿一条狭窄的江边路绕开封闭的桥。

examples.en: The team circumvented the broken sensor with a manual control.
examples.cn: 团队用手动控制绕过了失灵的传感器。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses take one geometry, the circle around a barrier, through roads, laws, questions, controls, opponents, taxes, technical fixes and system limits.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把「绕障一圈」这一几何用到道路、法规、难题、管控、对手、税费、技术补救与系统限制上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a truck turns off the main road and slips past the checkpoint on a side track.
core.cn: 核心意象：货车拐离主路，沿侧道滑过检查点。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL DETOUR: a barrier stands on the road and the route bends around it.
branches.cn: 空间绕行：障碍立在路上，路线在它外侧弯过去。

branches.en: THE RULE DODGED: a law or a charge has an edge that the arrangement never touches.
branches.cn: 规则被闪开：法规或收费有一道边缘，安排从不触碰。

branches.en: THE OBSTACLE LEFT ALONE: a hard question is skipped, or a faulty part is worked around.
branches.cn: 障碍被搁在一边：难题被跳过，或失灵部件被绕开。

branches.en: THE WATCHED LINE: a filter or a supervisor is defeated without being switched off.
branches.cn: 被盯的线：过滤或监管没有被关掉，却失效了。

branches.en: THE STRONG POINT AVOIDED: an opponent's position or a technical limit is passed on the side.
branches.cn: 强点被避开：对手的阵地或技术的限制从侧边过去。

intro.en: Circumvent is a Latin compound of a prefix meaning around and a verb meaning to come, and both pieces recur across English.
intro.cn: 这是一个拉丁复合词，由表示「周围」的前缀与表示「来」的动词构成，两部分在英语里都反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies circum, venire and circumvenire; the pieces are well recorded, so no part of this word is marked uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 circum、venire、circumvenire；这些部件有清楚记录，因此这个词没有哪一部分标为存疑。

items.exampleCN: 这个分词提供了英语形容词词干。

definition_zh: adj. 细菌学的；与细菌研究有关的；（引申）以细菌为手段的
definition_en: Relating to bacteriology, the study of bacteria; of methods or weapons that use bacteria.
core_image: 培养皿、显微镜与检验单构成的那一整套学问
scene: 实验室做过细菌学检测，确认水源没有污染。 The lab ran bacteriological tests and cleared the water supply.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bacteriological 指与细菌学这门研究有关的。

pos.zh: 细菌学的；以细菌为手段的

forms.label: 形容词原级（无屈折变化）

senses.title: Of the science of bacteria
senses.definition: belonging to bacteriology, the branch of biology that studies bacteria
senses.definitionCN: 属于细菌学，即研究细菌的生物学分支
senses.example: She published a bacteriological survey of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 她发表了一份关于那条河的细菌学调查。
senses.why: The word stacks bacterio-, small rod, with -logy, study, and -ical, relating to, so it means of the study of bacteria.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把 bacterio-「小棍」、-logy「学问」与 -ical「与……有关的」叠在一起，因此意为「与细菌研究有关的」。

senses.title: Using bacteria as a means
senses.definition: of tests, weapons or processes that work by means of bacteria rather than by studying them
senses.definitionCN: 指依靠细菌本身而非研究细菌来发挥作用的检测、武器或工艺
senses.example: The treaty bans bacteriological weapons.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约禁止细菌武器。
senses.why: Because the science handles the organisms, its adjective came to label anything that puts them to work.
senses.whyCN: 因为这门科学处理这些微生物，它的形容词便用来标记任何把它们投入使用的事物。

intro.en: Bacteriological is bacteriology plus -ical; bacteriology joins Greek bakterion, a small staff, with -logia, study, and was coined in the 1880s.
intro.cn: bacteriological 是 bacteriology 加 -ical；bacteriology 由希腊语 bakterion「小棍」与 -logia「学问」组成，于 1880 年代造出。

items.en: Greek bakterion meant a small staff, a diminutive of bakteria, a walking stick.
items.cn: 希腊语 bakterion 意为「小棍」，是 bakteria「手杖」的指小形式。

items.en: Naturalists took the word as bacterium for rod-shaped microbes seen under the lens.
items.cn: 博物学者借该词作 bacterium，指镜下所见的杆状微生物。

items.en: Greek -logia meant an account or study, from logos, word or reason.
items.cn: 希腊语 -logia 意为「论述、学问」，出自 logos「言辞、理性」。

items.en: Bacteriology was coined in the 1880s as the new discipline took shape.
items.cn: 随着这门新学科成形，bacteriology 于 1880 年代造出。

items.en: The adjective followed within a decade, used of tests and laboratories.
items.cn: 形容词在十年内随之出现，用于检测与实验室。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word gained the sense of using bacteria as weapons.
items.cn: 二十世纪这个词获得「以细菌为武器」之义。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the bacterium family; the near-meaning group lists other adjectives of the life sciences.
note.cn: 形近组保留 bacterium 词族；近义组列出生命科学的其他形容词。

entries.definitionCN: 研究细菌的学科。

entries.definition: A specialist in bacteria.
entries.definitionCN: 细菌方面的专家。

entries.definition: Relating to bacteria themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 与细菌本身有关的。

entries.definition: Relating to living things.
entries.definitionCN: 与生物有关的。

entries.definitionCN: 微生物研究的。

entries.definition: Relating to microbes.

entries.definition: Relating to disease processes.
entries.definitionCN: 与疾病过程有关的。

entries.definition: Free of living microbes.
entries.definitionCN: 无活微生物的。

normalIntro.en: Bacteriological is bacterio plus logy plus ical: relating to the study of the little rods.
normalIntro.cn: bacteriological 是 bacterio 加 logy 加 ical：与研究那些「小棍」有关的。

normal.en: Bacterial is of bacteria; bacteriological is of the science.
normal.cn: bacterial 指细菌本身，bacteriological 指这门科学。

normal.en: The noun is bacteriology, the person bacteriologist.
normal.cn: 名词是 bacteriology，人是 bacteriologist。

normal.en: Tests and analysis are the commonest nouns after it.
normal.cn: 其后最常见的名词是 tests 与 analysis。

normal.en: Bacteriological warfare is a set term.
normal.cn: bacteriological warfare 是固定术语。

normal.en: The shorter bacteriologic also exists.
normal.cn: 较短的 bacteriologic 也存在。

abstract.en: Picture a rack of dishes under a lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象灯下一排培养皿。

abstract.en: Imagine a report clearing a village well.
abstract.cn: 想象一份为村中水井开绿灯的报告。

abstract.en: Think of a science turned into a weapon.
abstract.cn: 想象一门科学被变成武器。

examples.en: Bacteriological tests confirmed the source.
examples.cn: 细菌学检测确认了来源。

examples.en: The hospital opened a bacteriological unit.
examples.cn: 医院开设了一个细菌学部门。

examples.en: Bacteriological contamination closed the beach.

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：bacterio「小棍、细菌」+ logy「学问」+ -ical「……的」——与细菌这门学问有关的，就是 bacteriological。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses belong to the same discipline: describing the study of bacteria, and describing what puts bacteria to use.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项同属一门学科：描述对细菌的研究，以及描述把细菌投入使用的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dishes, a microscope and a test report as one body of learning

branches.en: Tests clearing a water supply.

definition_zh: 河流的；沿河的；河岸的；河流生态的
definition_en: relating to a river, to its banks, or to the plants and animals that live in and along it
core_image: 一条河穿过干旱平原，两岸的树、堤路和村庄被它拉成一条细长的绿带
scene: 洪水退去后，两岸的村庄开始修补被冲坏的堤坝。 The riverine villages rebuilt the dikes that line both banks after the flood.
sceneCN: 这里 riverine 指「沿河而设、依河而居的」（第 2 个义项：沿河、河岸的）；句意：洪水过后，沿河的村庄重修了两岸的堤坝。图中可辨识物件：两岸堤坝、柳树、村庄屋顶、退水留下的泥痕。

senses.title: Of a river itself
senses.titleCN: 河流本身的，属于河流的
senses.definition: belonging to a river as a watercourse, or produced by the action of flowing water
senses.definitionCN: 属于作为水道的一条河流，或由流水作用产生的
senses.example: Riverine currents sort the gravel into long bars.
senses.exampleCN: 河流的水流把砾石分选成长条状的砾石坝。
senses.why: the adjective is built on Latin rivus 'stream', so its first job is to qualify the channel and the water in it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词建于拉丁 rivus「溪流」之上，因此首要功能是修饰河道与其中的水。

senses.title: Along the banks of a river
senses.definition: situated on or beside the banks of a river, or organised around the river's edge
senses.definitionCN: 位于河岸之上或河岸旁边，或以河岸为中心组织起来的
senses.example: The riverine villages rebuilt the dikes that line both banks after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后，沿河的村庄重修了两岸的堤坝。
senses.why: from the water the adjective moves to the land beside it, because a river's edge is where people build and plant.
senses.whyCN: 形容词由水面转向旁边的陆地，因为河岸正是人们建房与耕种的地方。

senses.title: The river-and-floodplain ecosystem
senses.definition: the habitat formed by a river together with its floodplain, including the species that depend on seasonal flooding
senses.definitionCN: 河流与其洪泛区共同构成的生境，包括依赖季节性泛滥的物种
senses.example: Riverine forests survive on the silt that spring floods spread across their roots.
senses.exampleCN: 河岸林靠春汛铺到根部的淤泥存活。
senses.why: ecology treats channel and floodplain as one unit, so the adjective names a system rather than a single line.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把河道与洪泛区视为一个单元，因此这个形容词命名的是一套系统，而不只是一条线。

senses.title: Landforms shaped by running water
senses.titleCN: 由流水塑造的河川地貌
senses.definition: the landforms and deposits produced by a river, such as terraces, bars and levees
senses.definitionCN: 由河流造成的地形与沉积，如阶地、砾石坝与天然堤
senses.example: Riverine terraces mark the older, higher courses of the stream.
senses.exampleCN: 河流阶地标出这条溪流更古老、更高的河道。
senses.why: geomorphology extends the adjective from the water to the shapes the water has left behind.
senses.whyCN: 地貌学把这个形容词从水扩展到水留下的形状。

senses.title: Riparian settlement and culture
senses.definition: the people, settlements and ways of life that cluster along a river
senses.definitionCN: 沿河聚居的人群、聚落与生活方式
senses.example: Riverine communities share boats, nets and a common calendar of floods.
senses.exampleCN: 河岸社区共享船只、渔网以及一套共同的洪水历法。
senses.why: a river is a road and a larder, so the adjective also describes the human life that grows along it.
senses.whyCN: 河流既是道路也是食源，因此这个形容词也描述沿河生长的人类生活。

senses.title: Transport by river
senses.definition: the movement of goods or passengers along a river rather than by road or rail
senses.definitionCN: 沿河道而非经公路或铁路运送货物或旅客
senses.example: Riverine transport is cheaper than road haulage along this stretch.
senses.exampleCN: 在这一段，河流运输比公路货运便宜。
senses.why: the channel is a route, so the adjective qualifies a mode of transport that uses the water as its road.
senses.whyCN: 河道是一条路线，因此这个形容词修饰一种把水当路用的运输方式。

senses.title: Flood hydrology and river regime
senses.definition: the seasonal behaviour of a river's flow, including floods, low water and sediment load
senses.definitionCN: 河流流量的季节变化，包括洪水、枯水与输沙
senses.example: Riverine flooding is predicted from snowpack and spring rainfall.
senses.exampleCN: 河流洪水依据积雪与春季降雨来预测。
senses.why: hydrology uses the adjective for the river's own behaviour in time, not for a place beside it.
senses.whyCN: 水文学用这个形容词指河流自身随时间变化的行为，而非旁边的地点。

senses.title: Life that lives in or by the river
senses.titleCN: 河生生物（生活在河中的生物）
senses.definition: organisms adapted to life in flowing fresh water or on its banks
senses.definitionCN: 适应在流动淡水中或河岸上生活的生物
senses.example: Riverine insects lay their eggs on stones that stay wet all year.
senses.exampleCN: 河生昆虫把卵产在常年湿润的石头上。
senses.why: the habitat sense narrows to its inhabitants, as with marine and terrestrial, which likewise name both realm and biota.
senses.whyCN: 生境义收窄到其中的居民，正如「海洋的」与「陆地的」这类词同样既指领域又指生物。

intro.en: Riverine is a nineteenth-century English formation: Latin rivus 'small stream' plus the adjective suffix -ine. It is not derived from English river, which came through Old French riviere from Latin ripa 'bank'. The two Latin words are different, and the similarity of the English forms hides that.
intro.cn: riverine 是 19 世纪英语造出的词：拉丁 rivus「小溪」加形容词后缀 -ine。它并非由英语 river 派生；river 经古法语 riviere 来自拉丁 ripa「河岸」。这两个拉丁词并不相同，只是英语词形相近，掩盖了这一区别。

items.en: Rivus meant 'small stream, brook'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the common reconstruction from an Indo-European root meaning 'to flow, run' is a reconstructed form, not a attested ancestor.
items.cn: rivus 意为「小溪、溪流」。其更深来源不确定；通常拟出的、意为「流动、奔跑」的印欧语词根属重构形式，并非有书证可查的祖形。

items.en: Ripa meant 'bank, shore' and is the source of English river through Old French riviere. River and riverine therefore look related but descend from different Latin nouns, a distinction that historical dictionaries make explicit.
items.cn: ripa 意为「河岸、岸」，经古法语 riviere 成为英语 river。因此 river 与 riverine 看似同族，实则出自不同的拉丁名词，历史词典对此有明确区分。

items.en: The suffix -ine, from Latin -inus 'belonging to', was already productive in English adjectives such as marine and feline when riverine was formed.
items.cn: 后缀 -ine 出自拉丁 -inus「属于……的」；在 riverine 造出时，它已能产于 marine、feline 这类英语形容词。

items.en: Riverine was coined in the nineteenth century, most likely in geographical and natural-history writing, to supply an adjective for the river and its banks; the exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: riverine 于 19 世纪造出，最可能出现在地理与博物学写作中，用来为河流及其两岸提供一个形容词；确切的最早书证年代不确定。

items.en: In the twentieth century ecology and hydrology adopted the word for whole river-floodplain systems and for a river's seasonal behaviour, which is why it now appears in technical compounds.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪，生态学与水文学采用该词指整个河流—洪泛区系统以及河流的季节性行为，因此它如今多见于技术性复合词。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first date): rivus has no settled Indo-European etymology, and the earliest English use of riverine is not precisely dated; the Latin base itself, however, is certain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与首见年代）：rivus 没有定论的印欧语词源，riverine 最早的英语用例也缺乏确切年代；但它的拉丁词基本身是确定的。

note.en: Group one separates riverine from look-alikes, above all English river, which descends from Latin ripa and is not its base; group two places it beside the other adjectives of wetland science.
note.cn: 第一组把 riverine 与形近词分开，尤其是英语 river——它出自拉丁 ripa，并非 riverine 的词基；第二组把它与湿地科学中的其他形容词并列。

entries.definition: English river comes through Old French riviere from Latin ripa 'bank, shore', not from rivus 'stream'; it is the everyday noun that riverine describes, but not its morphological base.
entries.definitionCN: 英语 river 经古法语 riviere 来自拉丁 ripa「河岸、岸」，而非 rivus「溪流」；它是 riverine 所描述的日常名词，却不是其构词词基。

entries.definition: From Latin rivulus, a diminutive of rivus, so it is a genuine cousin; it means a small stream, not a river bank.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 rivulus，是 rivus 的指小形式，因此确为同族；意为小溪，而非河岸。

entries.definition: From Latin rivalis, originally one who draws water from the same stream; the root is rivus, but the modern meaning is a competitor.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 rivalis，原指从同一条溪流取水的人；词根是 rivus，但今义为竞争者。

entries.definition: A deep narrow valley, from Latin rapina 'violent seizure'; it sounds like riverine but belongs to a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 指深邃狭窄的谷地，来自拉丁 rapina「强夺」；读音近似 riverine，但词根不同。

entries.definition: Of rivers and the action of flowing water, from Latin fluvius 'river'; it is the geological and technical counterpart of riverine.
entries.definitionCN: 指河流以及流水作用的，来自拉丁 fluvius「河流」；是 riverine 在地质与技术语境中的对应词。

entries.definition: Relating to the banks of a river, from Latin ripa; it overlaps with riverine in the bank sense but is rooted in ripa, not rivus.
entries.definitionCN: 指与河岸有关的，来自拉丁 ripa；在河岸义上与 riverine 重叠，但词根是 ripa 而非 rivus。

entries.definition: Of lakes, from Latin lacus; it is the lake equivalent of riverine in the classification of wetland and water habitats.
entries.definitionCN: 指湖泊的，来自拉丁 lacus；在湿地与水域生境分类中，它是 riverine 的湖泊对应词。

entries.definition: Of marshes, from Latin palus; in the same classification it names the marsh class beside riverine and lacustrine.
entries.definitionCN: 指沼泽的，来自拉丁 palus；在同一分类体系中，它与 riverine、lacustrine 并列，指沼泽类。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: rivus 'stream' plus -ine 'of': 'of a stream' is the core reading, not 'of a river bank'.
normal.cn: rivus「溪流」加 -ine「属于」：核心读法是「溪流的」，而不是「河岸的」。

normal.en: False-friend alert: river comes from ripa 'bank', while riverine comes from rivus 'stream'; the English spellings hide two different Latin nouns.
normal.cn: 易错点提醒：river 出自 ripa「岸」，riverine 出自 rivus「溪流」；英语拼写掩盖了两个不同的拉丁名词。

normal.en: The -ine wetland family lines up as riverine, riparian, lacustrine and palustrine: river, bank, lake, marsh.
normal.cn: 以 -ine 结尾的湿地词族可排成 riverine、riparian、lacustrine、palustrine：河流、河岸、湖泊、沼泽。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the applied senses: riverine ecosystem, riverine landscape, riverine transport.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出应用义：河流生态系统、河川景观、河流运输。

normal.en: Rival descends from the same rivus: two people who share one stream end up competing for its water.
normal.cn: rival 也出自同一个 rivus：共用一条溪流的人，最终会为水而竞争。

abstract.en: Picture a green thread stitched along a dry brown cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绿线，沿着干燥的棕色布面缝下去。

abstract.en: Picture houses standing in a single row because the water decides where they may stand.
abstract.cn: 想象房屋排成一列，因为水决定了它们只能站在哪里。

abstract.en: Picture a road and a river running side by side, each carrying what the other cannot.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路与一条河并排延伸，各自运送对方运不了的东西。

examples.en: Riverine forests survive on the seasonal flood that spreads silt across their roots.
examples.cn: 河岸林靠季节性洪水把淤泥铺到根部而存活。

examples.en: The riverine villages moved their kitchens and boats to the higher bank.
examples.cn: 沿河的村庄把厨房和船只搬到了较高的河岸上。

examples.en: Riverine transport is cheaper than road haulage along this stretch.
examples.cn: 在这一段，河流运输比公路货运便宜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「riverine」读似「瑞沃润」——河两岸被水润着，所以 riverine 就是沿河的、河岸的

root: 拉丁 rivus「小溪、溪流」+ 英语后缀 -ine（19 世纪仿拉丁 -inus 造词）；rivus 的印欧来源一般拟为 *rei-，属重构形式。注意：英语 river 出自拉丁 ripa「河岸」经古法语 riviere，与 riverine 并非同一词根。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line of water: the stream itself, the bank beside it, the river-floodplain system, the landforms it builds, the settlements along it, the traffic on it, the floods it sends, and the life adapted to it. The adjective keeps moving outward from the channel to everything the channel shapes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条水线展开：溪流本身、旁边的河岸、河流—洪泛区系统、流水造出的地貌、沿河的聚落、河上的运输、河流带来的洪水，以及适应它的生物。这个形容词不断由河道向外扩展，指向河道所塑造的一切。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow ribbon of water and trees drawn across dry country.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条水与树构成的细带，画在干旱的大地上。

branches.en: OF THE RIVER ITSELF: the adjective qualifies the channel and its flowing water.
branches.cn: 河流本身：这个形容词修饰河道与其流水。

branches.en: OF THE BANK: the same adjective shifts from the water to the land beside it.
branches.cn: 河岸：同一个形容词由水面转向旁边的陆地。

branches.en: OF THE SYSTEM AND ITS SHAPE: ecology and geomorphology treat river and floodplain as one unit.
branches.cn: 系统与形状：生态学与地貌学把河流与洪泛区视为一个单元。

branches.en: OF PEOPLE AND TRAFFIC: settlement and transport follow the bank line.
branches.cn: 人与交通：聚落与运输都沿着河岸线展开。

branches.en: OF FLOOD AND LIFE: the flood that builds the habitat is also the hazard, and the biota depends on both.
branches.cn: 洪水与生命：造出生境的洪水也是灾害，而生物同时依赖这两面。

intro.en: Riverine is a Latin root plus an English adjective suffix. The root rivus is also visible in rivulet and rival, while the suffix -ine recurs across wetland science in lacustrine and palustrine.
intro.cn: riverine 由一个拉丁词根加一个英语形容词后缀构成。词根 rivus 也见于 rivulet 与 rival；后缀 -ine 则在 lacustrine、palustrine 等湿地科学词汇中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin rivus 'stream' yields rivulus, the source of rivulet, and rivalis, the source of rival. Latin ripa 'bank' is a different noun and yields English river; the two Latin families must not be merged.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 rivus「溪流」衍生 rivulus，即 rivulet 的来源，也衍生 rivalis，即 rival 的来源。拉丁 ripa「岸」是另一个名词，衍生英语 river；两个拉丁词族不可合并。

items.example: Rivus is the base of the whole riverine family.
items.exampleCN: rivus 是整个 riverine 词族的词基。

items.meaning: belonging to; of the nature of
items.example: The suffix turns a noun into an adjective of belonging.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成表示归属的形容词。

items.meaning: of a stream or its banks
items.example: Riverine silt built the low terrace.
items.exampleCN: 河流带来的淤泥堆成了低阶地。

items.example: A rivulet ran under the stone bridge.
items.exampleCN: 一条小溪从石桥下流过。

items.meaning: one who shares the same stream; a competitor
items.meaningCN: 共用同一条溪水的人；竞争者
items.example: Two rivals drew from the same channel.
items.exampleCN: 两个竞争者从同一条水道取水。

items.meaning: of a river bank; note the different Latin base
items.meaningCN: 河岸的；注意其拉丁词基不同
items.example: Riparian willows hold the bank together.
items.exampleCN: 河岸的柳树把岸固定在一起。

items.example: Lacustrine deposits fill the old basin.
items.exampleCN: 湖泊沉积填满了古老的盆地。

items.example: Palustrine soils stay saturated all summer.
items.exampleCN: 沼泽土壤整个夏天都保持饱和。

items.meaning: a continuous strip of river habitat
items.example: The riverine corridor links the upland forest to the delta.
items.exampleCN: 河流廊道把高地森林与三角洲连接起来。

definition_zh: 宇宙的；巨大的；至关重要的
definition_en: relating to the cosmos; huge in scale or significance
core_image: X 射线天文望远镜拍到的星系碰撞图，配着人类尺度下的一双手示意大小
scene: 纪录片里解说员说： The collision of two galaxies is a cosmic event that plays out over hundreds of millions of years.
sceneCN: 这里指「宇宙尺度上的」（第1个义项）；句意为两个星系的碰撞是一个在几亿年间展开的 cosmic 事件。

pos.zh: 宇宙的；巨大的；至关重要的

senses.title: Relating to the cosmos or outer space
senses.titleCN: 与宇宙或外太空有关的
senses.definition: the core scientific sense; anything that happens beyond Earth and its atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 核心科学义项：地球和大气层以外发生的任何事
senses.example: Cosmic radiation constantly bombards the upper atmosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙辐射不断轰击高层大气。
senses.why: cosmic = of the cosmos, just like galactic = of a galaxy.
senses.whyCN: cosmic = 宇宙的，就像 galactic = 星系的。

senses.title: On an immense scale
senses.definition: informal usage: so large or so huge that it dwarfs normal human-scale numbers or events
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法：大到超过人类日常尺度的数字或事件
senses.example: The budget gap was cosmic — billions of dollars over what anyone had projected.
senses.exampleCN: 预算缺口是 cosmic 的——比任何人预期的多几十亿美元。
senses.why: Like astronomical, cosmic can refer to things on the scale of the universe.
senses.whyCN: 和 astronomical 一样，cosmic 可以指宇宙尺度的东西。

senses.title: Cosmic dust, rays, background radiation
senses.titleCN: 宇宙尘、宇宙射线、宇宙背景辐射
senses.definition: scientific compounds: cosmic describes anything in space — dust, rays, noise, microwave background
senses.definitionCN: 科学复合词：cosmic 描述太空里的一切——尘、射线、噪声、微波背景
senses.example: Cosmic microwave background radiation is the echo of the Big Bang.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙微波背景辐射是大爆炸的回声。
senses.why: The adjective is widely attached to nouns in astronomy and astrophysics.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词在天文和天体物理里广泛跟名词搭配。

senses.title: Cosmic importance or significance
senses.definition: used for events or decisions that seem as important as anything in the universe
senses.definitionCN: 用于重要得像宇宙里最关键的事件或决定
senses.example: To a child, losing a favourite toy can feel of cosmic importance.
senses.exampleCN: 对小孩来说，丢了最喜欢的玩具可能觉得是 cosmic 级别的事。
senses.why: Hyperbole borrows the largest scale to mean the most important.
senses.whyCN: 夸张借最大的尺度来指最重要的。

senses.title: Cosmic justice or cosmic order
senses.definition: used to describe a moral or natural order that is larger than human society
senses.definitionCN: 用来描述比人类社会更大的道德或自然秩序
senses.example: Some people believe in cosmic justice that balances the wrongs of this life.
senses.exampleCN: 有些人相信 cosmic 正义会平衡这一世的冤屈。
senses.why: Cosmic carries the 'ordered whole' sense from its Greek root kosmos.
senses.whyCN: Cosmic 带着希腊语词根 kosmos 的「有序整体」含义。

senses.title: Cosmic vs astronomical vs galactic
senses.definition: cosmic = whole universe; astronomical = of astronomy or huge; galactic = of galaxies; the scales grow smaller
senses.definitionCN: cosmic = 整个宇宙；astronomical = 天文学的或巨大的；galactic = 星系的；尺度逐个变小
senses.example: Cosmic events span billions of galaxies; galactic events span one galaxy.
senses.exampleCN: Cosmic 事件跨越几十亿星系；galactic 事件只跨一个星系。
senses.why: The progression maps nicely: cosmic > astronomical > galactic.
senses.whyCN: 这个阶梯很清楚：cosmic > astronomical > galactic。

senses.title: Cosmic in popular culture and New Age
senses.titleCN: 流行文化和新世纪运动里的 cosmic
senses.definition: used for anything feeling mystical, universal or out of the ordinary
senses.definitionCN: 用来指神秘的、普遍的或不普通的事物
senses.example: The festival had a cosmic vibe — everyone felt connected to something bigger.
senses.exampleCN: 那个节日有一种 cosmic 的氛围——人人觉得和更伟大的东西连上了。
senses.why: New Age culture picked up cosmic because it evokes vastness, mystery and unity.
senses.whyCN: 新世纪运动喜欢 cosmic 因为它唤起浩瀚、神秘、合一。

senses.title: Cosmic rays and particle physics
senses.definition: high-energy particles from space that hit Earth's atmosphere; studied by particle physicists
senses.definitionCN: 来自太空、轰击地球大气的高能粒子；由粒子物理学家研究
senses.example: Cosmic rays discovered new fundamental particles before accelerators could.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙射线在加速器之前就发现了新的基本粒子。
senses.why: Cosmic rays are nature's own particle accelerator — cheaper and more powerful than anything we can build.
senses.whyCN: 宇宙射线是大自然自己的粒子加速器——比我们能造的都便宜且强大。

intro.en: cosmic is the adjective of cosmos: Greek kosmos (ordered universe) + -ic adjective suffix.
intro.cn: cosmic 是 cosmos 的形容词：希腊语 kosmos（有秩序的宇宙）+ -ic 形容词后缀。

items.en: kosmos 'order, ornament, universe' → cosmic via Latin and French.
items.cn: kosmos「秩序、装饰、宇宙」→ 经拉丁语和法语 → cosmic。

items.en: cosmic appeared in English in the early 17th century, borrowed from Latin cosmicus.
items.cn: cosmic 17 世纪早期进入英语，借自拉丁语 cosmicus。

items.en: With the growth of astrophysics in the 20th century, cosmic became attached to dozens of scientific compounds.
items.cn: 20 世纪天体物理成长时，cosmic 与几十个科学复合词搭在一起。

items.en: The 'huge scale' sense developed alongside astronomical and galactic in the 20th century.
items.cn: 「巨大尺度」的义项在 20 世纪和 astronomical, galactic 一起发展起来。

items.en: New Age writers and musicians adopted cosmic in the 1960s and 1970s.
items.cn: 1960-70 年代新世纪作家和音乐人采用 cosmic。

items.en: Scientific, figurative and New Age senses all remain active.
items.cn: 科学、比喻、新世纪的义项今天都活跃。

note.cn: 第一组共享 cosm- 词根；第二组把 cosmic 和其他尺度形容词对比。

entries.definition: The noun that cosmic describes.
entries.definitionCN: cosmic 描述的那个名词。

entries.definition: Study of the cosmos; cosmic events are often studied here.
entries.definitionCN: 宇宙学；cosmic 事件常在其中研究。

entries.definition: One who studies cosmology.
entries.definitionCN: 宇宙学家。

entries.definition: Study of how the cosmos began.
entries.definitionCN: 宇宙起源论。

entries.definition: Huge in scale; of astronomy. Overlaps strongly with cosmic.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大尺度的；天文学的。与 cosmic 强烈重叠。

entries.definition: Of galaxies; smaller than cosmic, bigger than stellar.
entries.definitionCN: 星系的；比 cosmic 小，比 stellar 大。

entries.definition: Of stars themselves; smaller than galactic or cosmic.
entries.definitionCN: 恒星本身的；比 galactic 或 cosmic 小。

entries.definition: Applying everywhere; different angle from cosmic's 'scale' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 到处适用的；与 cosmic 的「尺度」义角度不同。

normalIntro.cn: cosmic = 宇宙的。

normal.en: cosmos + -ic = cosmic, just like physics + -ic = physic (archaic for physical).
normal.cn: cosmos 加 -ic 构成 cosmic。

normal.en: Cosmic rays come from outer space.

normal.en: The cosmic microwave background is the echo of the Big Bang.

normal.en: A cosmic event is so big it dwarfs everything else.
normal.cn: 一个 cosmic 事件大到其他一切都渺小。

normal.en: Cosmic justice balances the wrongs of the whole universe.
normal.cn: 宇宙正义平衡整个宇宙的冤屈。

abstract.en: The quiet hum of radiation left over from the beginning.
abstract.cn: 开端留下的辐射的安静嗡嗡声。

abstract.en: Something vast, ancient, and indifferent — that still gives us our atoms.
abstract.cn: 浩瀚、古老、冷漠的存在——但给了我们身上的每一个原子。

abstract.en: A word that can describe a supernova or a song, a budget gap or a love affair.
abstract.cn: 一个可以描述超新星或一首歌、预算缺口或一段爱情的词。

examples.en: Cosmic dust is one of the key ingredients for forming new stars and planets.
examples.cn: 宇宙尘是形成新恒星和行星的关键成分之一。

examples.en: To a four-year-old, finding their lost teddy bear feels of cosmic importance.
examples.cn: 对四岁小孩来说，找到丢失的泰迪熊感觉是 cosmic 级别的事。

examples.en: The team detected a burst of cosmic rays that could not be explained by known sources.
examples.cn: 团队探测到一次无法用已知来源解释的宇宙射线爆发。

definition_zh: 社会阶层；社会等级；阶级（社会学概念）
definition_en: a group of people ranked together by income, occupation, education and standing, or the system of such rankings
core_image: 同一栋楼里，不同楼层的人用不同的电梯，孩子们上不同的学校
scene: 同一条街的两端，信箱里的信件来自不同的学校与不同的诊所。 Social class shaped who survived the epidemic and who was merely ill.
sceneCN: 这里 social class 指与阶层位置相关的结果差异（第 5 个义项：与阶层相关的结果差异）；句意为社会阶层决定了谁能熬过这场疫病，谁只是生病。

pos.zh: 社会阶层；社会等级（可数，指某一阶层；不可数，指分层现象）

derivatives.zh: 等级；类别（拉丁 classis「民众的划分」，由划分转指类别本身）
分类（class + -ify「使成为」，由类别转指归类的动作）
无阶层的（class + -less「无」，由阶层转指其缺失）
使社会化；交际（social + -ize，由社会关系转指使之进入关系）

senses.title: The system of ranks
senses.definition: the whole arrangement by which a society ranks its members in tiers
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会把成员分成层级的整套安排
senses.example: Social class is inherited more often than it is chosen.
senses.exampleCN: 社会阶层多半是继承的，而非选择的。
senses.why: the compound names a structure rather than one rung, so it is used for the system itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词组命名的是结构而非一级阶梯，因此用于体系本身。

senses.title: One tier of people
senses.definition: a group sharing roughly similar income, occupation and education
senses.definitionCN: 收入、职业与教育大致相近的一群人
senses.example: The town had three social classes and one road.
senses.exampleCN: 这个镇子有三个阶层和一条路。
senses.why: counting tiers requires a countable noun, and the compound supplies one.
senses.whyCN: 要数层级，就需要可数名词，这个词组正好提供。

senses.title: The criteria of rank
senses.definition: the measures, such as income, schooling or occupation, used to place people
senses.definitionCN: 用来给人定位的尺度，如收入、学历或职业
senses.example: Social class in that survey meant income and schooling only.
senses.exampleCN: 在那份调查里，社会阶层只指收入与学历。
senses.why: every ranking needs a yardstick, and the phrase can name the yardstick instead of the result.
senses.whyCN: 任何排序都需要尺子，这个词组可以指尺子而非结果。

senses.title: Class identity
senses.definition: the sense of belonging to a tier and of sharing its interests
senses.definitionCN: 对某一层级的归属感与共享利益之感
senses.example: Social class became visible when the factory closed.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂关门时，社会阶层就显形了。
senses.why: a rank becomes a social fact when people act on it, so the phrase also names awareness.
senses.whyCN: 当人们据此行动时，等级就成了社会事实，因此这个词组也指意识。

senses.title: Class-linked outcomes
senses.titleCN: 与阶层相关的差异结果
senses.definition: differences in health, schooling and life expectancy that follow rank
senses.definitionCN: 随等级出现的健康、学业与寿命差异
senses.example: Social class predicts the diagnosis more accurately than the postcode.
senses.exampleCN: 社会阶层比邮编更能预测诊断结果。
senses.why: researchers needed a term for the pattern, not for the persons, and this is it.
senses.whyCN: 研究者需要一个词指这个模式而非人，这个词组正是。

senses.title: Mobility between tiers
senses.definition: movement upward or downward between classes across a lifetime or generations
senses.definitionCN: 一生或数代之间在阶层间的上下移动
senses.example: Social class still limits how far a scholarship can carry a student.
senses.exampleCN: 社会阶层仍限制着奖学金能把学生送多远。
senses.why: mobility is measured against class, so the phrase names the frame that movement crosses.
senses.whyCN: 流动是相对阶层来衡量的，因此这个词组命名被穿越的那个框架。

senses.title: Upper, middle, lower
senses.definition: the familiar three-tier vocabulary used in everyday description
senses.definitionCN: 日常描述中常见的三层说法
senses.example: The labels upper, middle and lower still organize social class in speeches.
senses.exampleCN: 上层、中层、下层这些标签仍组织着演讲里的社会阶层。
senses.why: the phrase carries the inherited three-tier scheme even when data do not fit it.
senses.whyCN: 即使数据不合，这个词组仍带着继承下来的三层图式。

senses.title: An analytic category
senses.definition: a variable used in sociological models to explain inequality
senses.definitionCN: 社会学模型中用来解释不平等的变量
senses.example: The paper treats social class as a variable, not a verdict.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文把社会阶层当作一个变量，而不是判决。
senses.why: the analytic sense deliberately strips the phrase of moral tone so it can be measured.
senses.whyCN: 分析义刻意剥去道德语气，以便它可以被测量。

intro.en: Social class joins social, from Latin socius 'companion', to class, from Latin classis 'a division of the Roman people'. The compound is a modern coinage. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: social class 把 social 与 class 接在一起：social 来自拉丁 socius「同伴」，class 来自拉丁 classis「罗马民众的划分单位」。整个词组是近代产物。年代均为约数。

items.en: Socius meant 'companion, ally', from a root for following; socialis 'of a companion or an alliance' produced social.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴、同盟者」，其词根含「跟随」之意；socialis「同伴的、结盟的」产生 social。

items.en: Classis named a division of the Roman people for voting and military service, and also a fleet. Its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: classis 指罗马民众按投票与兵役所分的等级，也指舰队。其更深来源未得到证明。

items.en: English class first meant a group of students, then a category, and only later a social rank.
items.cn: 英语 class 先指一批学生，再指类别，最后才指社会等级。

items.en: Social entered English through French in the sixteenth century, meaning 'of society or of companions'.
items.cn: social 在 16 世纪经法语进入英语，意为「社会的、同伴的」。

items.en: Social class became a fixed phrase in nineteenth-century writing on industrial society, when rank ceased to be fixed by birth alone.
items.cn: social class 在 19 世纪论工业社会的著述中成为固定说法，当时等级不再只由出身决定。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the first use of the exact phrase is not precisely dated, and the origin of classis is unsettled, so forms proposed for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：这一确切词组的首用没有精确年代；classis 的来源亦无定论，为其提出的形式属重构形式。

note.en: Group one gathers words built on class or close in form; group two holds terms for social ranking.
note.cn: 第一组是以 class 构成或形近的词；第二组是社会分层的术语。

entries.definition: A category, a school group or a rank; social class specifies the rank in a whole society.
entries.definitionCN: 类别、班级或等级；social class 限定为整个社会中的等级。

entries.definition: From Latin classicus 'of the highest class of citizens', a derivative of classis; it means exemplary, not social rank.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 classicus「最高等级公民的」，是 classis 的派生；意为典范的，而非社会等级。

entries.definition: To sort into categories; it shares the class stem but says nothing about hierarchy.
entries.definitionCN: 按类别分开；共享 class 词干，却不涉及等级。

entries.definition: Of society or interaction, from socius; alone it carries no rank.
entries.definitionCN: 指社会或交往的，来自 socius；单独使用不含等级义。

entries.definition: A hereditary rank closed to outsiders, as in the Indian system; social class is usually open in principle.
entries.definitionCN: 由出身决定、对外封闭的等级，如印度制度；social class 原则上通常可流动。

entries.definition: A composite index of income, education and occupation; it is the quantitative cousin of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 收入、教育与职业的合成指数；是这一词组的定量表亲。

entries.definition: A single layer in a ranked society, used in sociology for one tier rather than the system.
entries.definitionCN: 分层社会中的单层，社会学用来指一级而非体系。

entries.definition: A person's position as judged by others; it is individual where social class is collective.
entries.definitionCN: 他人所评定的个人位置；属个人，而 social class 属群体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: classis was a division of the Roman people, so class began as a slice of a population.
normal.cn: classis 是罗马民众的划分单位，因此 class 本是一块人口切片。

normal.en: socius 'companion' + -alis: social means of companions, and class adds the ranking.
normal.cn: socius「同伴」+ -alis：social 指同伴之间的，class 再加上等级。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: working-class background, class divide, social mobility.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：工人阶级出身、阶层鸿沟、社会流动。

normal.en: The family runs class, classify, classic, classless, social, socialize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 class、classify、classic、classless、social、socialize。

normal.en: Compare the trio: class is the short word, social class the society-wide rank, caste the closed version.
normal.cn: 比较三个：class 是短词，social class 是全社会的等级，caste 是封闭版。

abstract.en: Picture a building where the lift buttons are labelled by income.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋楼，电梯按钮按收入标注。

abstract.en: Picture two children born a street apart and never in the same classroom.
abstract.cn: 想象两个相差一条街出生的孩子，从未同班。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder whose rungs are visible only when someone climbs.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子，只有有人攀爬时横档才显形。

examples.en: Social class still decides which school a child can reach.
examples.cn: 社会阶层仍决定一个孩子能上哪所学校。

examples.en: The study found social class mattered more than the hospital.
examples.cn: 研究发现社会阶层比医院更重要。

examples.en: He wrote about social class without ever naming his own.
examples.cn: 他写社会阶层，却从不提自己属于哪一层。

dict_mnemonic.text: social（社会的）+ class（等级）＝ 社会里的那几级台阶；记「同一条街，不同的学校」。

root: social：拉丁 socius「同伴」+ -alis「……的」；class：拉丁 classis「罗马民众的划分单位」，其更深来源不确定；整个词组为 19 世纪固定说法。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses go from structure to measurement: the ranking system, one tier, the yardstick, the sense of belonging, the outcomes that follow rank, movement across ranks, the everyday three-tier labels, and the sociologist's variable.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从结构走到测量：分层体系、某一层级、划分尺度、归属意识、随等级而来的结果、跨层流动、日常的三层标签，以及社会学家的变量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one street whose two ends send their children to different schools and their sick to different clinics.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一条街的两端，孩子上不同的学校，病人去不同的诊所。

branches.en: FRAME AND LABELS: the whole ranking, then the familiar upper-middle-lower shorthand.
branches.cn: 框架与标签：先是整套排序，再是上中下的日常简称。

branches.en: UNIT AND RULER: one tier of people, and the measures that put them there.
branches.cn: 单位与尺子：一层人，以及把他们放上去的尺度。

branches.en: THE INSIDE VIEW: rank becomes real when people feel they belong to it.
branches.cn: 内部视角：当人们感到自己属于某一层，等级才成真。

branches.en: CAUSE AND ESCAPE: outcomes follow rank, and mobility is the attempt to leave it.
branches.cn: 因果与逃逸：结果随等级而来，流动则是试图离开它。

branches.en: THE VARIABLE: analysis turns the phrase into something measurable.
branches.cn: 变量：分析把这一词组变成可测量之物。

intro.en: Social class is a two-word phrase: social is a Latin adjective from socius, class a Latin noun from classis, and each half builds its own family.
intro.cn: social class 是两词短语：social 是由 socius 来的拉丁形容词，class 是由 classis 来的拉丁名词，两半各有自己的词族。

latinIntro.en: Socius gives social, society, associate and sociable; classis gives class, classic and classify.
latinIntro.cn: socius 衍生 social、society、associate、sociable；classis 衍生 class、classic、classify。

items.example: Socius is the base of social.
items.exampleCN: socius 是 social 的基础。

items.example: Socialis passed through French as social.

items.meaning: a division of the people; a fleet
items.example: Classis named a voting division.
The word narrowed from divisions to ranks.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从划分收窄为等级。

items.example: A classic is a work of the first rank.
They classify the records by decade.

definition_zh: 废奴主义者；主张废除某项制度的人；形容词：废奴主义的
definition_en: a person who campaigns for the abolition of slavery or another institution; also the adjective describing such a position
core_image: 印刷机旁堆着刚印好的小册子，墙上钉着请愿名单，一只手正把传单递给路人
scene: 街角的小印刷铺里，油墨未干的小册子摞在木箱上，几个人把传单塞给过路人，墙上贴满请愿名单。 The abolitionist, a campaigner for ending slavery, printed a thousand pamphlets before the debate.
sceneCN: 这里 abolitionist 指「主张废除奴隶制的活动者」（第 1 个义项：为废奴而行动的人）；句意为这位废奴主义者在辩论前印了一千份小册子。可辨识物件：印刷机、小册子、木箱、请愿名单、递出的传单。

pos.zh: 废奴主义者；主张废除某项制度的人（可数，复数 abolitionists）
废奴主义的；主张废除的（作定语，如 abolitionist press）

senses.title: A campaigner against slavery
senses.definition: a person who worked to end slavery and the slave trade
senses.definitionCN: 为结束奴隶制与奴隶贸易而奔走的人
senses.example: The abolitionist printed a thousand pamphlets before the debate.
senses.exampleCN: 这位废奴主义者在辩论前印了一千份小册子。
senses.why: abolition plus -ist names the person who seeks the ending of an institution, and the first institution in question was slavery.
senses.whyCN: abolition 加 -ist 命名争取终止制度的人，而当时首先针对的制度就是奴隶制。

senses.title: A member of an organised movement
senses.definition: someone belonging to a society, party or network dedicated to abolition
senses.definitionCN: 隶属于致力于废除的协会、党派或网络的人
senses.example: Abolitionists met every Tuesday in the back room.
senses.exampleCN: 废奴主义者每周二在后屋聚会。
senses.why: a cause that organizes turns supporters into members, and the agent noun marks that role.
senses.whyCN: 组织起来的事业把支持者变成成员，施动名词标示这一角色。

senses.title: An advocate of ending any institution
senses.titleCN: 主张废除任何制度的人
senses.definition: by extension, a person who campaigns to end a practice such as a tax, a prison system or a monarchy
senses.definitionCN: 引申指为终止某项做法而奔走的人，如某项税、监狱制度或君主制
senses.example: Prison abolitionists borrowed the word from the antislavery struggle.
senses.exampleCN: 监狱废除论者从反奴隶制斗争中借用了这个词。
senses.why: the suffix is productive: any institution can gain an -ist who wants it gone.
senses.whyCN: 这个后缀能产：任何制度都能得到一个想让它消失的 -ist。

senses.title: A supporter of an abolitionist organ
senses.titleCN: 废奴主义报刊或组织的支持者
senses.definition: a reader, funder or writer attached to an abolitionist newspaper or society
senses.definitionCN: 与废奴报刊或协会相关的读者、资助者或撰稿人
senses.example: The paper's abolitionists raised money for the press.
senses.exampleCN: 这家报纸的废奴主义支持者为印刷机筹款。
senses.why: movements need infrastructure, and the noun also labels those who sustain it.
senses.whyCN: 运动需要基础设施，这个名词也标示维持它的人。

senses.title: A historical type
senses.definition: the recognised nineteenth-century figure studied in histories of the Atlantic slave trade
senses.definitionCN: 大西洋奴隶贸易史研究中公认的十九世纪人物类型
senses.example: Historians compare British and American abolitionists.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家比较英国与美国的废奴主义者。
senses.why: when a movement becomes history, its members become a social type with shared tactics and vocabulary.
senses.whyCN: 当运动成为历史，其成员就成为具有共同策略与语汇的社会类型。

senses.title: The adjective use
senses.definition: describing a newspaper, society, argument or position as belonging to abolitionism
senses.definitionCN: 描述报纸、协会、论点或立场属于废奴主义
senses.example: The abolitionist press reached readers in three states.
senses.exampleCN: 废奴主义报刊的读者遍及三个州。
senses.why: English often lets agent nouns work as modifiers without any change of form.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让施动名词不加变化地充当修饰语。

senses.title: By extension: one who urges cancellation
senses.titleCN: 比喻：主张取消某项做法的人
senses.definition: a person who argues that a practice should be scrapped rather than reformed
senses.definitionCN: 主张某项做法应被取消而非改良的人
senses.example: The manager became an abolitionist about the weekly report.
senses.exampleCN: 这位经理成了每周报告的「废除派」。
senses.why: the metaphor contrasts abolition with reform: one ends the thing, the other repairs it.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把「废除」与「改良」对照：一个终止事物，一个修补事物。

senses.title: Abstraction: an advocate of erasure
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：主张抹除制度的人
senses.definition: anyone who seeks the complete removal of a structure rather than its adjustment
senses.definitionCN: 任何寻求彻底移除某一结构而非调整它的人
senses.example: An abolitionist is a reformer who refuses to keep the frame.
senses.exampleCN: 废奴主义者是拒绝保留框架的改革者。
senses.why: the deepest sense is a stance toward institutions: not improve them but end them.
senses.whyCN: 最深的一层是对制度的态度：不是改良，而是终结。

intro.en: Abolitionist is an English formation from abolition plus the agent suffix -ist, though a French parallel exists. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: abolitionist 是英语由 abolition 加施动后缀 -ist 构成，法语中也有平行形式。年代均为约数。

items.en: The word is built inside English from abolition and the agent suffix -ist, which marks a person devoted to a cause.
items.cn: 这个词在英语内部由 abolition 与施动后缀 -ist 构成，后者标示投身某项事业的人。

items.en: French abolitionniste is a close parallel formed at about the same time; whether English borrowed it or coined its own is not settled.
items.cn: 法语 abolitionniste 是大约同时形成的平行词；英语是借用还是自造，尚无定论。

items.en: The suffix goes back through Latin -ista to Greek -istēs, an agent ending used for adherents of a practice or school.
items.cn: 这个后缀经拉丁 -ista 上溯希腊 -istēs，是用来指某种实践或学派追随者的施动词尾。

items.en: The word is recorded in the 1780s and 1790s, when campaigns against the slave trade were organizing in Britain and France.
items.cn: 这个词见于十八世纪八九十年代，当时英法的反奴隶贸易运动正在组织起来。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the term was extended to campaigns against other institutions, such as capital punishment.
items.cn: 在十九、二十世纪，这个词被扩展到反对其他制度的运动，如废除死刑。

items.en: Source uncertain (first attestation and borrowing path): dictionaries do not agree on the earliest use, and the French-or-English origin of the English word remains open.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与借入路径）：辞书对最早用例说法不一，英语词究竟源自法语还是英语自造仍无定论。

note.en: Group one holds abolition-family words easily confused with the person noun; group two holds neighbouring roles in reform.
note.cn: 第一组是易与这个人物名词混淆的废除类词；第二组是改革中的邻近角色。

entries.definition: The ending of an institution; an abolitionist is the person who seeks that ending.
entries.definitionCN: 指终止制度的行为；abolitionist 是寻求这一终止的人。

entries.definition: The body of belief and activity behind abolition; the -ist is one adherent of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指废除背后的信念与活动体系；-ist 是其中一名追随者。

entries.definition: One who seeks the freeing of enslaved people; abolitionists sought to end the institution itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指寻求使被奴役者获自由的人；废奴主义者则寻求终止制度本身。

entries.definition: Describing measures that abolish; it is not a noun for a person.
entries.definitionCN: 描述具有废除作用的措施；不是指人的名词。

entries.definition: Anyone who campaigns for change; abolitionist specifies the change sought.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何为改变而奔走的人；abolitionist 具体说明所寻求的改变。

entries.definition: A person who runs a sustained public effort; the word names the activity, not the aim.
entries.definitionCN: 指开展持续公共行动的人；这个词命名活动，而非目标。

entries.definition: Opposed to slavery; it can describe a newspaper or a voter without naming a profession of activism.
entries.definitionCN: 指反对奴隶制的；可描述报纸或选民，而不指职业活动者。

entries.definition: One who seeks to improve an institution; an abolitionist wants it ended instead.
entries.definitionCN: 指寻求改良制度的人；废奴主义者则要终止它。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the base noun, the agent suffix and the historical campaign.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：基础名词、施动后缀与历史运动。

normal.en: abolition + -ist: the person who works for the ending.
normal.cn: abolition + -ist：为终止而努力的人。

normal.en: -ist goes back to Greek -istēs, a person attached to a practice or school.
normal.cn: -ist 上溯希腊 -istēs，指依附某种实践或学派的人。

normal.en: The family runs abolish, abolition, abolitionism, abolitionist, abolitionary.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 abolish、abolition、abolitionism、abolitionist、abolitionary。

normal.cn: 这场运动定在十八世纪八九十年代，最先针对奴隶贸易。

normal.en: The word also works as an adjective: abolitionist press, abolitionist society.
normal.cn: 这个词也作形容词：废奴主义报刊、废奴协会。

examples.cn: 这位废奴主义者主张自由劳动也更有生产力。

examples.cn: 废奴主义者在若干港口城市遭遇暴力。

examples.cn: 展览纪念一位基本被遗忘的废奴主义者。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings move from the person who fought slavery, through the movement member and the extended campaigner, to the supporter of a press, the historical type, the adjective, and finally the general advocate of cancellation and of erasure.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从反对奴隶制的人出发，经过运动成员与扩展的活动者，再到报刊支持者、历史类型、形容词用法，最后落到一般主张取消者与主张抹除者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: inky pamphlets stacked by a press, a petition on the wall and a leaflet held out to a stranger.
core.cn: 核心意象：印刷机旁堆着油墨未干的小册子，墙上是请愿书，一只手把传单递给陌生人。

branches.en: THE PERSON AND THE BODY: an individual campaigner and an organised member share the name.
branches.cn: 个人与团体：个体活动者与组织成员共用这个名称。

branches.en: THE EXTENDED CAUSE: any practice can find its own abolitionist.
branches.cn: 扩展的事业：任何做法都能找到自己的废除派。

branches.en: THE INFRASTRUCTURE AND THE RECORD: a press needs supporters, and history turns them into a type.
branches.cn: 设施与记录：报刊需要支持者，历史把他们变成类型。

branches.en: THE MODIFIER: the same form works as an adjective before a noun.
branches.cn: 修饰语：同一形式可在名词前作形容词。

branches.en: THE STANCE: the deepest sense is a refusal to keep the frame.
branches.cn: 立场：最深的一层是拒绝保留框架。

intro.en: Abolitionist is a transparent derivative: a Latin-derived base noun plus a Greek-derived agent suffix.

latinIntro.en: The base abolition goes back to Latin abolere and abolitio; the suffix -ist reaches English through Latin -ista from Greek -istēs.
latinIntro.cn: 基础词 abolition 上溯拉丁 abolere 与 abolitio；后缀 -ist 经拉丁 -ista 从希腊 -istēs 进入英语。
